The second: Imam al-Razi said: Know that the purpose of mentioning the stories of the prophets, peace be upon them, is that a lesson be obtained by whoever hears them. It is as if God, when He mentioned the story of Adam and showed in it the severity of Satan's enmity toward Adam and his offspring, followed it by warning his offspring against accepting Satan's whispering, saying: "O children of Adam" [al-A'raf: 26], and that is because when Satan's effect of his plotting, the subtlety of his whispering, and the intensity of his concern reached the point that he was able to cast Adam into the lapse that necessitated his removal from Paradise, then he is all the more able to bring about similar harms against the children of Adam.

By this method, God warned the children of Adam to guard against his whispering.

His saying, exalted is He: "Indeed, he sees you, he and his soldiers": i.e., his troops of devils, "from where you do not see them": i.e., from a place in which you do not see them.

The sentence is a resumptive clause giving the reason for the prohibition and emphasizing the warning against his temptation, since he is like an enemy who conceals himself, plotting against you and assassinating you from where you are unaware. It is related from Malik ibn Dinar: "Indeed, an enemy who sees you while you do not see him is severely burdensome, except for whom God protects."

Note: al-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: Ibn al-Faras said: Some scholars have used it as evidence that the jinn cannot be seen, and whoever says they can be seen is a disbeliever.

By "some" he means the Mu'tazilites. Therefore al-Zamakhshari said: In it is clear evidence that the jinn are not seen and do not appear to mankind, that their manifesting themselves is not within their capability, and that the claim of one who asserts seeing them is a falsehood and a fabrication. End.

Al-Jashani said: It indicates the invalidity of the common view that Satan appears to us and that we see him. Then he said: If it is asked, "Are they not seen in the time of the prophets, and does the one witnessing see the angel?" our answer is that the intensity of the ray increases or their bodies become condensed, so it becomes a miracle for the Prophet. End.

The People of the Sunnah answered, as in al-'Inayah: their being seen has been established by well-known authentic hadiths, and these do not contradict what is in the verse, because what is negated in it is their being seen when they do not take shape for us.

In Fath al-Bayan it says: A group of scholars have used this verse as evidence that seeing Satan is impossible, but there is nothing in the verse indicating that. The most that it says is that he sees us from where we do not see him, and it does not say that we never see him at all, for the negation of our seeing him at the time of his seeing us does not entail negation of seeing him absolutely.

The truth is the permissibility of their being seen, as is the apparent meaning of the authentic hadiths, and the verse is to be understood as specific to them, so that they are seen at some times by some people and not by others. End.

Al-Ghazali, may God have mercy on him, clarified the seeing of the jinn and the devils by the seeing of the angels, where he said in (the Second Pillar): The angels, the jinn and the devils are substances subsisting in themselves, differing in their realities by a difference that exists between species. Then he said: It is possible for these substances — I mean the substances of the angels — to be witnessed, although they are not perceptible to the senses.

This witnessing is of two kinds: either by way of representation, as in God's saying: "So she took the form for her of a well-proportioned man" [Maryam: 17], and as the Prophet, prayers and peace be upon him, used to see Gabriel in the form of Dihya al-Kalbi.

(p-2651) The second kind: that some angels have a particular body, just as our souls are not perceptible, yet they have a perceptible body which is the locus of their activity and their own particular world. Likewise some angels. Perhaps this perceptible body is dependent on the illumination of the light of prophethood, just as the perceptible things of this world of ours are dependent, for perception, on the illumination of the light of the sun. Likewise with the jinn and the devils. End.

His saying, exalted is He: "Indeed, We have made the devils allies to those who do not believe." Al-Zajjaj said: That is, We empowered them over them, and they increase them in their error. End. This sentence is another reason for the prohibition, and it contains a warning more emphatic than the first.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿And when they commit an abomination, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it." Say, "Indeed, Allah does not command abomination. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?"﴾

﴿And when they commit an abomination﴾ — i.e., a sin whose ugliness has reached its extreme, such as polytheism and exposing the private parts during circumambulation (p-2652). ﴿They say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it."﴾ — i.e., when they did these things, they offered as excuse that their fathers used to do them, so they followed them, and that Allah commanded them to do them, since He approved of them in it; for had He disliked it, He would have forbidden them from it. Both of these are false: the first is the imitation (taqlid) of the ignorant, and imitation is not a path to knowledge; the second is a fabrication against the Majestic One.

Al-Shihab said: In His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Allah has commanded us﴾, there is an implied omitted possessive, i.e., "commanded our fathers," so one does not say that the apparent meaning is that they were commanded to do it. The departure from the apparent meaning is a sign of their claim that their fathers' command was a command to them.

﴿Say, "Indeed, Allah does not command abomination."﴾ — i.e., what you do is a heinous abomination, and Allah does not command the like of it, because His, glorified and exalted is He, established custom is to command good deeds and urge noble qualities. ﴿Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?﴾ This is a denunciation of their attributing the command of abomination to Him, glorified is He; it includes a prohibition against fabricating about Him, exalted is He, and in it is a testimony that the basis of their saying is extreme ignorance.

Al-Shihab said: There is no proof in the verse for one who negates analogy (qiyas), on the basis that what is established by it is conjectural (maznun), not certain, because its generality is specified by the consensus of the Companions and those whose opinion is considered, or by another proof.

Note:

Mujahid said: The polytheists used to circumambulate the House naked, saying, "We circumambulate as our mothers bore us." A woman would place upon her private part a strip of leather or something else and say:

"Today some of it or all of it appears, and what appears of it, I do not make lawful."

So Allah revealed: ﴿And when they commit an abomination﴾ to the end of the verse. Ibn Kathir said: The Arabs, other than the Quraysh, did not circumambulate the House in the clothes they wore, interpreting that they should not circumambulate in garments in which they had disobeyed Allah. The Quraysh — and they are the Hums — used to circumambulate in their own clothes; whoever was lent a garment by a Hamsi (Hums member) circumambulated in it, and whoever had a new garment circumambulated in it and then discarded it, so no one would take possession of it; and whoever did not find a new garment, nor was lent one by a Hamsi, (p-2653) circumambulated naked. Perhaps it would be a woman, who would circumambulate naked, placing upon her private part something to cover it partially, and she would say: "Today it appears..." — the House... And most women used to circumambulate at night. This was something they had innovated of their own accord and followed their fathers in, believing that their fathers' practice was grounded in a command from Allah and a law. So Allah, exalted is He, denounced them for that.

Al-Suyuti mentioned in (al-Iklil), from Ibn Abbas as well, that it was revealed concerning their circumambulating the House naked; Abu al-Shaykh and others narrated it. He said: In it is the obligation of covering the private parts during circumambulation.

Two notes:

The first: The Mu'tazilah held that will (irada) is the implication of the command and necessarily accompanies it, and abomination — by which I mean evils and sins — is not commanded, by the explicit text of the verse, and so it is not willed by Him, exalted is He.

The people of the Sunnah answered that the command may be separated from will, in the sense that it exists without will, so will is not consequent upon it in existence. What clarifies that a thing may be commanded without being willed is that when a master wishes to show his disobedience to those present, he commands his slave to do something without willing it from him. Also, the command is of two kinds:

A creative command (amr takwini), by which the existence of things comes about, which is the address "Be" (kun), and it follows will and encompasses all created beings. Thus obediences and disobediences are all commanded and willed by this command, and obedience, disobedience, reward and punishment are not connected to this command, because it relates to things in the state of non-existence.

And a legislative command (amr tashri'i tadwini), i.e., what Allah legislated for His servants and charged them with, what has been recorded and explained in the books of the Shari'ah. This command is connected to obedience, disobedience, reward, punishment, approval and displeasure; disbelief and sins are not commanded by this command.

The Mu'tazilah did not distinguish between the two commands, and said: If disbelief and sins were willed by Allah, exalted is He, they would be commanded, and performing what is commanded is obedience, so the disbeliever and the wrongdoer would be obedient, for they are commanded to do them by the first command, and they are not commanded to do them by the second command, so that their performing them would be obedience.

(p-2654) Al-Sayalkuti said: Your not being unaware of the division of the command into two commands is only valid if His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82], is taken in its apparent sense, as some have held. But if it is an expression for bringing into existence without an address being connected to it, as al-Ash'ari and those who followed him held, then this does not hold. End.

The matter is elaborated in its known places.

The second: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Say, "Indeed, Allah does not command abomination."﴾ is an answer to their second false claim.

He did not mention an answer to the first, and al-Imam said: because it is an indication of pure imitation, and it has been established by reason that it is a corrupt method, since imitation occurs in contradictory religions. If imitation were true, it would necessitate affirming the truth of contradictory religions; since its corruption is evident, He, exalted is He, did not mention it.

The third: In Fath al-Bayan it is said: In this noble verse is the greatest deterrent and most eloquent admonition for the imitators who follow their fathers in doctrines opposed to the truth, for that is from following the people of disbelief, not the people of truth. For they are the ones who say: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 23], and those who say: ﴿We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it﴾. The imitator, were it not for his being deceived by the fact that he found his fathers upon that doctrine, together with his belief that it is what Allah commanded and that it is the truth, would not remain upon it. This trait is what kept the Jew upon his Judaism, the Christian upon his Christianity, and the innovator upon his innovation. Nothing kept them upon these misguidances except that they found their fathers in Judaism, Christianity and innovation, and they thought well of them, that what they were upon is the truth which Allah commanded, and they did not look to themselves, nor did they seek the truth as it must be sought, nor did they investigate Allah as He should be investigated. This is pure imitation and utter deficiency. Then he said: Among the most wondrous heedlessness and the greatest oblivion of the truth is the choice of the imitators of the opinions of men (p-2655), while the Book of Allah exists, the Sunnah of His Messenger exists among them, one who takes both from him exists before them, the instrument of understanding is available to them, and the faculty of reason is with them. End.

When He negated what they had attributed to Him, and informed that He does not command abomination, He explained what He commanded, by His saying, exalted is He:

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[29] ﴿Say: My Lord has commanded justice. And set your faces upright at every place of prostration, and call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion. As He originated you, [so] you will return.﴾

﴿Say: My Lord has commanded justice﴾ "That is, with equity (al-'adl). The early scholars (al-salaf) have several interpretations here: what has been recognised by the intellects as good; or monotheism (al-tawhid); or the word of sincerity (kalimat al-ikhlas). And from Abu Muslim: all acts of obedience (al-ta'at). Al-Hakim said: and this is the (preferred) view. It is not hidden that all of these are encompassed by (al-qist), so there is no contradiction."

﴿And set your faces upright at every place of prostration﴾ This is coordinated with the command that the verbal noun (al-masdar) resolves into along with (an) [i.e., "that"]. That is: "by [being] equitable and by setting up," and the verbal noun may be resolved into the past, the present, and the imperative, as the grammarian (al-mu'rib) transmitted. Or it is coordinated with "My Lord has commanded": that is, "Say: set up."

Al-Jurjani said: the command is coordinated with the report, because what is intended is its wording, or because it is an act of speech (insha') in meaning. End of quotation.

"The faces" (al-wujuh) is a metaphor for the persons (al-dhawat). "Masjid" is either a verbal noun, with the time understood before it, and "'inda" in the sense of "fi" (in), meaning: set your persons upright in every time of prostration, by restraining them from turning to others during it, and by observing conformity to the command together with sincerity of intention; or by facing the qibla during it. Or it is a noun of time or place in the linguistic sense, meaning: at every time of prostration or its place.

Prostration (al-sujud) on these interpretations is a metaphor for prayer (al-salat); or "masjid" is the term in its technical use, and the meaning is: at whatever masjid prayer reaches you, and do not delay it until you return to your mosques. The command on this reading is for recommendation (al-nadb); it was said that this does not suit the context. But if it is taken with what precedes it, it is for obligation (al-wujub).

These interpretations are derived from what has been narrated from the early scholars. In (al-Lubab) it says: the meaning of the verse, according to Mujahid and al-Suddi, is: direct your faces wherever you are in prayer toward the Ka'bah. Al-Dahhak said: the meaning is that when prayer comes and you are at the masjid, then pray in it, and let none of you say: "I pray in my masjid" or "the masjid of my people." It was also said its meaning is: make your prostration purely for Allah.

﴿And call upon Him﴾ "That is: worship Him. ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾ "That is: the obedience, by dedicating it to Him, because He has deserved your worship by bringing you into being, and you cannot forgo it, since to Him is your return in the Hereafter. ﴿As He originated you, [so] you will return﴾ "That is: just as He created you at the beginning, He will return you to Him living, and He will recompense you for your deeds, so make your worship sincerely for Him. He likened the return to the beginning only to establish its possibility and the power to do it."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 7, verse 30:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[30] ﴿A group He guided, while a group had error decreed upon them. Indeed, they took the devils as allies instead of Allah, and they think that they are guided.﴾

﴿A group He guided﴾ by granting them success in faith. ﴿And a group had error decreed upon them﴾, and they are the disbelievers. ﴿Indeed, they took the devils as allies﴾, i.e., as helpers and lords, ﴿instead of Allah﴾, in that they obeyed them in what they commanded them of disbelief and sins. ﴿And they think that they are guided﴾, i.e., that they are upon guidance and truth in what they believe.

Two admonitions:

The first: Ibn Jarir said: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and they think that they are guided﴾ is among the clearest indications against the view of one who claims that Allah does not punish anyone for a sin he commits or an error he holds, unless he commits it after knowing the correct way of it, and so commits it out of defiance toward his Lord in it. For if that were so, there would be no difference between the group of error who went astray while thinking they were guided, and the group of guidance; yet Allah, exalted is He, has distinguished between their names and their rulings in this verse. End.

Its summary, as al-Qadi said, is that the verse indicates that the disbeliever who is mistaken and the defiant one are equal in deserving blame.

Al-Qadi said: The one who distinguishes may take it to refer to the one who is negligent in reflection; that is, the pronoun in "took" refers to the disbeliever who is negligent in reflection. As for those who strove and exerted their utmost effort, they are excused, as is the view of some scholars. Thus in (al-Inaya).

The second: Al-Razi said: This verse indicates that mere supposition and assumption do not suffice for the validity of religion; rather, certainty, decisiveness and conviction are required in it, because He, exalted is He, censured the disbelievers for their thinking that they were guided. Had this assumption not been blameworthy, He would not have censured them for it. End.

Al-Mahayimi said: Among what they supposed themselves to be guided in, by following the devil, is their abandoning adornment and enjoyment together with worship, so they circumambulated naked; and their abandoning meat and fat while in the state of ihram. Thus the Mighty and Majestic said:

**The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[31] ﴿O Children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prostration, and eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who are excessive.﴾

﴿O Children of Adam, take your adornment﴾: that is, clothing. ﴿At every place of prostration﴾: that is, every house built for worship. It may be understood as a noun of place, or as a verbal noun meaning prostration, intending by it prayer and worship, since worship is the most fitting time for adornment. ﴿And eat and drink﴾: during the days of Hajj, strengthening yourselves for worship. ﴿And do not be excessive﴾: that is, excess that leads to indulgence in desires and distracts from worship. Or it may mean: do not forbid the good things of provision, such as meat and fat. ﴿Indeed, He does not like those who are excessive﴾: the transgressors.

**Remarks:**

**The first:** As we mentioned earlier in the introduction to this tafsir, one of the benefits of knowing the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) is to grasp the meaning and remove ambiguity. We have only summarized the interpretation of this verse as we did because it was revealed concerning that matter.

[p-2658] Muslim related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The woman used to circumambulate the House while naked, saying: "Who will lend me a garment for circumambulation?" She would put it over her private parts and say:

*Today some or all of it appears,*
*And what appears of it, I do not make lawful.*

Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Take your adornment﴾, to the end of the verse. And the verse was revealed: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah...﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 32], to the end of the verse.

With Ibn Jarir, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: They used to circumambulate naked, the men by day and the women by night, and the woman would say:

*Today some or all of it appears,* ∗∗∗ *And what appears of it, I do not make lawful.*

Then ﴿Take your adornment﴾ was revealed. In al-Lubab, it is said: In another narration from him: Allah commanded them to wear their clothes and not to go naked.

Al-ʿAwfi related from Ibn ʿAbbas also, regarding the verse, who said: Some men used to circumambulate the House naked, so Allah commanded them to adornment. Adornment is clothing, which covers the private parts, and whatever else is good cloth and goods. So they were commanded to take their adornment at every place of prostration.

Abu al-Shaykh related from Tawus, who said: They were commanded to wear clothes. He related by another route from him that he said: The shamla (a wrap) [p-2659] is part of adornment.

Mujahid said: There was a tribe from the people of Yemen, and whenever one of them came as a pilgrim (hajj) or visitor (ʿumrah), he would say: "It is not proper for me to circumambulate in a garment in which I have disobeyed (Allah)." He would say: "Who will lend me a loincloth?" If he found one, he would wear it, and otherwise he circumambulated naked. So Allah revealed concerning this what you have heard: ﴿Take your adornment﴾, to the end of the verse.

Al-Zuhri said: The Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked, except the Hums (the Quraysh and their allies). Whoever came from outside the Hums would take off his clothes and circumambulate in a garment belonging to a member of the Hums. He thought it was not lawful for him to wear his own clothes. If he could not find someone from the Hums to lend him one, he would discard his clothes and circumambulate naked. If he circumambulated in his own clothes, he would discard them when he finished his circumambulation and make them harām (forbidden) for himself, meaning he made them unlawful for himself. Therefore Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of prostration﴾.

What is meant by adornment is the garments that cover the awrah (the parts that must be covered). Mujahid said: That which covers your private parts, even if it is an ʿabaʾah (a cloak). End of quotation.

Ibn Kathir said: This is what Mujahid, ʿAta', Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, Malik from al-Zuhri, and many other leading early scholars said in its interpretation: that it was revealed concerning the circumambulation of the polytheists around the House naked. End of quotation.

It is clear, then, that what is meant by adornment is that which covers the awrah, because that is the obligatory matter commanded, which the occasion of revelation clarifies, and not the adornment of beautification that comes to mind first. This is because what is derived from ﴿take﴾ (khudhu) is the obligation of taking, whereas wearing clothes for beautification is recommended (mashnun). This was said by al-Shihab. I say: The verse, by what its occasion of revelation indicates, shows that adornment (zinah) in the linguistic sense is not restricted to the good quality of clothing as is supposed. Al-ʿAwfi, from Ibn ʿAbbas, clarified this in what we have quoted.

In al-Tahdhib: Adornment is a comprehensive term for everything with which one adorns oneself. Similarly in al-Sihah and al-Qamus, and its wording is: Adornment is what one adorns oneself with.

Al-Harrani said: Adornment is the beautifying of a thing by means of something else, such as a garment, an ornament, or an appearance.

Al-Raghib said: True adornment is that which does not disgrace a person in any of his states, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. End of quotation.

Al-Razi related the consensus of the exegetes that what is meant by "adornment" is wearing clothes that cover the awrah.

[p-2660] He said: Adornment is not achieved except by complete covering of the awrahs. He also said: Allah, Exalted is He, said in the preceding verse: ﴿We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts and as adornment (riyash)﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 26]. So He made clear that clothing which covers the private parts is among the kinds of riyash (fine raiment) and adornment.

Then Allah, Exalted is He, commanded taking adornment in this verse, so it is necessary that what is meant by this adornment is what was mentioned in that verse. Furthermore, His saying ﴿take your adornment﴾ is a command, and a command implies obligation. Thus it is established that taking adornment is obligatory, and everything other than wearing clothes is not obligatory. Therefore it is necessary to interpret adornment as wearing clothes, acting upon the text as far as possible. And it cannot be said that His saying ﴿and eat and drink﴾ is a command of permission (amr ibahah), so the one preceding it would be the same, because abandoning the apparent meaning in the later clause does not necessitate abandoning it in the earlier clause.

Moreover, al-Hafiz Ibn Mardawayh related from the hadith of Saʿid ibn Bashir and al-Awzaʿi, from Qatadah, from Anas, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ): that it was revealed concerning prayer in sandals.

Abu al-Shaykh likewise related it from him, and from Abu Hurayrah a similar report. Ibn Kathir said: There is an issue regarding its authenticity, and Allah knows best.

I say: There is no issue, because that is among the things that adornment includes. We have mentioned in the introduction that the phrase "it was revealed concerning such-and-such" is not intended to mean that the ruling of the verse is restricted to that case, but rather that the verse is restricted to its category, so it includes whatever resembles it. So reflect on this.

There are very many hadiths on the legitimacy of praying in sandals. Among them: from Abu Maslamah Saʿid ibn Yazid, who said: "I asked Anas: Did the Prophet (ﷺ) pray in his sandals? He said: Yes." (Agreed upon.)

Al-ʿIraqi said in his commentary on al-Tirmidhi: Among those who used to do this, meaning wearing sandals in prayer, were ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan, ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, ʿUwaymir ibn Saʿidah, Anas ibn Malik, Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ, and Aws al-Thaqafi. Among the Successors (tabiʿun): Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, al-Qasim, ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah, ʿAta' ibn Yasar, ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, Mujahid, Tawus, Shuraih the judge, Abu Mijlaz, Abu ʿUmar al-Shaybani, al-Aswad ibn Yazid, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, Ibrahim al-Taymi, ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, and his son Abu Jaʿfar. End of quotation.

(p-2661) Abu Dawud related from the hadith of Abu Saʿid, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When one of you comes to the mosque, let him look, and if he sees filth or harm in his sandals, let him wipe it off and pray in them." And from the hadith of ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) praying barefoot and shod." Related by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah.

**The second:** The verse indicates the obligation of covering the awrah during circumambulation, because that was the occasion of revelation. They said: The wording also includes prayer, since it is performed in the mosque.

**The third:** Some have tried to derive from it the recommendation of beautifying oneself for prayer, saying: Since it indicates the obligation of taking adornment by covering the awrah in prayer, it is understood from it, in general, that it is good to beautify oneself by wearing what is good and beautiful in it.

Al-Kiya al-Harrasi said: The apparent meaning of the verse is the command to take adornment at every mosque, because of the virtue connected with it, in honor of the mosque and the acts performed in it, such as seclusion (iʿtikaf), prayer, and circumambulation.

Ibn al-Furs said: Malik used this verse as evidence for the disapproval of praying in the mosques of tribes without outer garments (ardiyah). Some of the early scholars used it as evidence that it is not permissible for a woman to pray without a necklace or two earrings. Thus in al-Iklil. The latter is an extreme of stretching the meaning.

Ibn Kathir said: By this verse and what has come in its meaning from the Sunnah, beautifying oneself at prayer is recommended, especially on Friday and on the day of ʿId. Perfume is also recommended, because it is part of adornment, and the siwak (tooth-stick), because it is part of completing that. Among the best clothing is white, because Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Wear white garments, for they are among the best of your clothes, and shroud your dead in them. Among the best of your kohl is antimony (ithmid), which clears the sight and makes the hair grow." And Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan related, from Samurah ibn Jundub, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Upon you are white garments; wear them, for they are purer and better, and shroud your dead in them." Al-Tabarani related with a sound chain, from Qatadah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, that Tamim al-Dari bought a cloak for a thousand (dirhams), and he used to pray in it.

**The fourth:** The connection of the command to take adornment with the command to eat and drink in His saying ﴿and eat and drink﴾ is what al-Kalbi related: "The Banu ʿAmir used not to eat during the days of their Hajj except plain food, and they did not eat fat, glorifying their Hajj by this. The Muslims said: 'We have more right to do this, O Messenger of Allah.' [p-2663] So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿and eat and drink﴾."

Al-Suddi said: Those who circumambulated the House naked used to forbid themselves fat as long as they were in the season. So Allah, Exalted is He, said to them: ﴿and eat and drink﴾, to the end of the verse.

**The fifth:** Excess (israf) was interpreted as exceeding the limit in what is permitted, which is by forbidding it. Al-Jashami al-Yamani said in his tafsir (al-Tahdhib): The verse indicates the prohibition of excess, and that is in two ways:

The first: spending on sin, such as boasting, games, adultery, wine, and the like. The second: exceeding the limits, and this varies according to wealth and poverty. For whoever has a small amount, if he spends it on hospitality, perfume, or silk garments, while he and his dependents need it, that is prohibited excess. Similarly for the wealthy, it is not disapproved and is not excess. It also indicates that things are permissible in principle, and reason indicates this, because Allah, Exalted is He, created them for their benefit, and the revealed texts came to confirm this. Therefore He said: ﴿Who has forbidden﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 32], demanding a revealed textual proof. End of quotation.

Imam Ahmad related from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Eat, drink, wear, and give charity, without arrogance or excess, for Allah loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His servant."

Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah related something similar.

Al-Bukhari said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Eat what you like and wear what you like, so long as two things do not befall you: excess (israf) or arrogance (makhilah)."

Ibn Jarir related it from him also with the wording: Allah permitted eating and drinking so long as they are not excess or arrogance.

Al-Shihab said: This (what Ibn ʿAbbas said) does not contradict what al-Tha'alibi and others among the men of letters mentioned: that a person should eat what he desires and wear what people desire, as it has been said:

*A counsel, a counsel,* ∗∗∗ *the wise have spoken by it:*
*Eat what you desire and wear* ∗∗∗ *what people desire.*

This is for abandoning what is not customary among people, and this is for the permissibility of all that they are accustomed to. Makhilah means arrogance. Ma here is durative and temporal (ma dawamiyyah zamaniyyah). Akhta'ataka comes from their saying: "So-and-so erred (akhta'a) in such-and-such," meaning he lacked it. In al-Asas: Among the metaphorical usages: "What has been written for you will not miss you (lan yukhti'aka)." And "The rain missed the land (akhta'a al-matar al-ardh)": it did not reach it. And "The arrows passed him (takhatta'athu al-nabl)": they went beyond him. End of quotation.

In His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He does not like the excessive﴾, there is a warning and a threat to whoever is excessive in these things, because whoever Allah does not love, He is not pleased with.

**The sixth point:** The exegetes and others have related what is said about the words of the Exalted, ﴿Eat and drink﴾ "…the verse," that it encompasses all of medicine. Its origin is what al-Zamakhshari and al-Kirmani related in their *'Aja'ib* (Marvels): Al-Rashid had a skilled Christian physician, who said to Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid, "There is nothing in your Book of the knowledge of medicine, and knowledge is of two kinds: knowledge of the bodies and knowledge of the religions." He replied, "Allah has encompassed all of medicine in half a verse of His Book." He asked, "And what is it?" He said, "The words of the Exalted: ﴿Eat and drink, but do not be excessive﴾." The Christian said, "Nothing has been related from your Messenger concerning medicine!" He replied, "Our Messenger (ﷺ) encompassed medicine in few words." He asked, "And what are they?" He said his saying: "The stomach is the house of disease, and restraint (*hima*, dietary regimen) is the head of medicine, and give every body what it is accustomed to." The Christian said, "Neither your Book nor your Prophet has left anything of medicine for Galen."

Al-Ayni said in *al-'Inaya*: "Some have omitted the completion of this story, because there is discussion among the scholars of hadith regarding the authenticity of this report."

In *Shu'ab al-Iman* by al-Bayhaqi, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The stomach is the basin of the body, and the veins come to it. When the stomach is sound, the veins issue forth with health, and when the stomach is corrupt, the veins issue forth with sickness." End of quotation.

I say: If this account is authentic, then the correct response of the Christian to his second question is refutation and falsehood, for there has been related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of the wonders of medicine and kinds of treatment what has not been related from any prophet ever. The scholars of hadith in the era of the early generations have a large section of it in their collections (*jawami'*) and musnads. As for the eminent later scholars, the abundance of what has been related on this subject compelled them to compile it in lengthy and abridged volumes under the title *al-Tibb al-Nabawi* (The Prophetic Medicine).

The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) has explained the inclusion of the principles of medicine in the Mighty Revelation, and the wonders of it in the Pure Sunnah, in a manner that astonishes minds, "and above every possessor of knowledge is One who knows" (12:76). He said, may Allah be pleased with him, in his book *Zad al-Ma'ad fi Hady Khayr al-'Ibad*:

*Chapter*

We have already covered some of his (ﷺ) guidance in the expeditions, biographies, dispatches, detachments, letters, and the letters he wrote to kings and their deputies. We follow that with useful chapters on his guidance in medicine, which he practised himself and prescribed to others, and we explain the wisdom in it, which most minds of most physicians fail to reach, and that the relation of their medicine to it is like the relation of the medicine of old women to theirs. So we say, and in Allah is the seeking of help:

Illness is of two kinds: illness of the hearts and illness of the bodies, and both are mentioned in the Qur'an.

Illness of the heart is of two kinds: illness of doubt and suspicion, and illness of desire and error, and both are in the Qur'an. The Exalted said regarding the illness of doubt: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased them in disease﴾ [al-Baqara: 10]. And the Exalted said: ﴿So that those in whose hearts is a disease and the disbelievers may say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 31]. And the Exalted said regarding those who were called to the judgment of the Qur'an and the Sunnah but refused and turned away: ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, behold, a party of them turn away﴾ [al-Nur: 48]. ﴿But if the right is theirs, they come to him willingly﴾ [al-Nur: 49]. ﴿Is there in their hearts a disease, or have they become doubtful, or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will be unjust to them? Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Nur: 50]. This is the illness of doubts and suspicions.

As for the illness of desires, the Exalted said: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women. If you fear Allah, then do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet, but speak in an honorable manner﴾ [al-Ahzab: 32]. This is the illness of the desire for fornication, and Allah knows best.

As for the illness of bodies, the Exalted said: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick﴾ [al-Nur: 61]. He mentioned the illness of the body in the Hajj, the fast, and the ablution for a wondrous secret, which demonstrates the greatness of the Qur'an and self-sufficiency in it for whoever understands and comprehends it, above anything else. That is because the rules of the medicine of bodies are three: preserving health, protection from what is harmful, and expelling corrupt matter. He, glory be to Him, mentioned these three principles in these three places. He said regarding the fast: ﴿So whoever among you is sick or on a journey, then [an equal number of] other days﴾ [al-Baqara: 184]. He permitted breaking the fast for the sick because of the excuse of illness, and for the traveller, seeking to preserve his health and strength, lest the fast in travel should diminish them, because of the combination of intense movement and what it entails of dissolution, and the lack of nourishment to replace what has dissolved, so strength becomes weak and diminishes. So He permitted the traveller to break the fast to preserve his health and strength from what weakens them.

He said regarding the Hajj: ﴿So whoever among you is sick or has an ailment of the head, then an expiation of fasting or charity or sacrifice﴾ [al-Baqara: 196]. So He permitted the sick, and whoever has an ailment in his head, such as lice or itching or other things, to shave his head while in the state of ihram, to expel the corrupt vapours which caused him harm in his head by their confinement under the hair. When he shaves his head, the pores open and those vapours come out of them. This expulsion is the measure by which every expulsion whose confinement causes harm is judged. The things whose confinement and resistance cause harm are ten: blood when it agitates, semen when it accumulates, urine, faeces, wind, vomit, sneezing, sleep, hunger, and thirst.

Each of these ten, its confinement causes one of the diseases by being held back. The Exalted has drawn attention, by the expulsion of the least of them, which is the vapour confined in the head, to the expulsion of what is more difficult than it, as is the way of the Qur'an: drawing attention from the lower to the higher.

As for the regimen (*hima*), He said regarding the verse of ablution: ﴿And if you are ill or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself, or you have touched women, and you find no water, then perform tayammum with clean earth﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 6]. So He permitted the sick to turn from water to dust, as a regimen for him so that his body does not suffer what harms him. This is a notice of the regimen against everything harmful to him, from within or from without. Thus the Exalted has guided His servants to the principles of medicine and the comprehensive foundations of its rules.

We mention the guidance of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) regarding that and explain that his guidance in it is the most perfect guidance.

As for the medicine of hearts, it is entrusted to the Messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, and there is no way to attain it except through them and at their hands. The soundness of hearts is that they should know their Lord and Creator, and His names, attributes, actions, and rulings, and that they should prefer His pleasure and what He loves, and avoid what He forbids and what angers Him.

There is no health for them nor life for them at all except by that, and there is no way to receive it except from the Messengers. What is thought of as the attainment of soundness of the heart without following them is an error on the part of whoever thinks that. That is only the life and health and strength of the bestial, desiring soul, and the life, health, and strength of the heart are far removed from that. Whoever does not distinguish between this and that, let him weep over the life of his heart, for he is among the dead, and over its light, for he is immersed in seas of darkness. End of quotation.

He, may Allah have mercy on him, has explained this station in another style in his book *Tariq al-Hijratayn*, which we also cite for the originality of its style. He said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Since the illness of the body is the opposite of its health and soundness, and it is the departure of the body from its natural balance by a corruption that befalls it, through which its perception and natural movement are corrupted, then either its perception goes away entirely, like blindness, deafness, or paralysis; or its perception diminishes due to weakness in the instruments of perception while its perception remains upright; or it perceives things contrary to what they are, as when one perceives sweet as bitter, and the foul as good, and the good as foul.

As for the corruption of its natural movement, it is like when its digestive, retentive, expulsive, or attractive power becomes weak.

So there arises for it pain in proportion to its departure from balance, but despite that it does not reach the limit of death and destruction; rather there remains in it some strength for perception and movement. The cause of this departure from balance is either corruption in quantity or in quality. The first is either a deficiency in the matter, requiring its increase, or an excess in it, requiring its decrease.

The second is either by an increase or decrease of heat or cold, or moisture or dryness, beyond the natural measure, so it is treated according to what that requires. The foundation of health rests on preserving strength, protection from what is harmful, and expelling corrupt matter, and the physician's judgment revolves around these three principles. The Mighty Book has included them, and guided to them He who sent it down as healing and mercy.

As for preserving strength, He, glory be to Him, commanded the traveller and the sick to break the fast in Ramadan and that the traveller make it up when he returns and the sick when he recovers, to preserve their strength for them. For the fast increases the sick in weakness, and the traveller needs to conserve his strength for the hardship of travel, so the fast weakens it.

As for protection from what is harmful, He, glory be to Him, protected the sick from using cold water in ablution and bathing if it harms him, and commanded him to turn to tayammum, as a protection for him from what is harmful reaching him from the outside of his body. How much more so from what is harmful to him within!

As for expelling corrupt matter, He, glory be to Him, permitted the muhrim who has an ailment of the head to shave it, so that shaving expels the harmful vapours to him. This is one of the easiest and lightest kinds of expulsion, and by it He drew attention to what he needs more than that.

I once discussed this with some heads of medicine in Egypt, and he said, "By Allah, if I had travelled to the West to know this benefit, it would have been a small journey," or as he said. End of quotation.

Then the Exalted refuted those who forbade some of the foods, drinks, and clothing of their own accord without any law from Allah, to emphasise what preceded, with His saying, glory be to Him.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 7, verse 32:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[32] ﴿Say: "Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good things of sustenance?" Say: "They are for those who believed in the life of this world, exclusively so on the Day of Resurrection." Thus We detail the signs for a people who know.﴾

﴿Say﴾: that is, to these polytheists who forbid what they forbid by their corrupt opinions and their innovations. ﴿Who has forbidden the adornment of God﴾: that is, of garments and everything else with which one beautifies oneself. ﴿which He has brought forth for His servants﴾: from plants, such as cotton and flax; from animals, such as silk and wool; and from minerals, such as armor. Thus the exegetes generalized here, and the reasoning is that restricting it would make what has already passed unnecessary. ﴿and the good things of sustenance﴾: that is, the delicious foods and drinks.

Al-Mahayimi said: That is, if they claim that adornment and enjoyment contradict humility, which is worship, and so are forbidden along with it, then He informs them that He has brought these forth for His servants whom He created to worship Him, so that they may adorn themselves with them during worship, like the conduct of servants of kings when they attend their service. This does not contradict their humility before Him. Likewise the good things, which He created to gladden the hearts of His servants so that they may give thanks to Him, and thanks is worship. Thus enjoyment does not contradict worship; rather it may even be a motive toward it. End of quotation.

(p-2671) Notes:

First: "The good things" has been explained as "the lawful," and as "meat and fat," which they used to forbid during the days of pilgrimage as mentioned earlier, and as "the bahira and the sa'iba," as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: "Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you have made from it what is unlawful and lawful?"﴾ [Yunus: 59]. It is evident that the wording of the verse is more general than that, although what was mentioned enters it in the first place, since the verse was revealed only to censure them regarding it, and the consideration is the generality of the wording.

Al-Razi said: The word "adornment" encompasses all kinds of beautification, including cleanliness of the body, mounts, and types of jewelry (meaning for women). Then he said: Under "the good things" enters everything that is enjoyed and desired among kinds of food and drink, and it includes enjoyment of women and perfume. The Prophet (ﷺ) rejected the intention of Uthman ibn Maz'un to castrate himself and to devote himself entirely to abstinence.

Second: The verse indicates that the basic ruling regarding foods, clothing, and all kinds of adornments is permissibility (ibaha), because the interrogative in "who" is for the emphatic denial of their prohibition, since denying the agent entails denying the act, for it does not exist without him.

Third: In the verse there is a refutation of those who scrupulously abstain from eating delicious foods and wearing fine garments, for there is no asceticism in abandoning the good of them. For this reason the verse came framed by an interrogative carrying denial against whoever forbids that for himself or forbids it for others. How excellent is what Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: "Indeed, he erred who preferred wearing hair and wool over wearing cotton and flax, while the path to the lawful is available, and whoever ate herbs and lentils and preferred them over the taste of wheat, and whoever abandoned eating meat out of fear of the onset of desire." End of quotation.

Fourth: Ibn al-Furs said: Whoever permitted men to wear silk and khazz (a fabric of silk and wool) has used this verse as evidence. Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Sinan ibn Salama that he used to wear khazz, and the people said to him: "Someone like you wears this?" He said to them: "Who is it that forbids the adornment of God which He has brought forth for His servants?" But Tawus transmitted that he recited this verse and said: "He did not command them with silk or brocade, but when one of them circumambulated the Ka'ba wearing his clothes, he was beaten and they were stripped from him." So said al-Iklil.

I say: That the verse does not include silk is clear enough without explanation, because what the evidence has specified is not covered by the general wording, and the hadiths on the prohibition of silk are too numerous to count. Therefore deriving its permissibility from them is rejected against the one who claims it.

﴿Say: they﴾: that is, the adornment of God and the good things are created ﴿for those who believed in the life of this world﴾ primarily, and the disbelievers, although they share in them, do so by following. ﴿exclusively so on the Day of Resurrection﴾: that is, no one else shares them with them, because God has forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers. The word "exclusively" is in the circumstantial accusative (hal), and it has been read in the nominative, meaning that it is a predicate following another predicate.

Subtle point:

Al-Mahayimi said: They were created for the believers so that they may know through them the pleasures of the Hereafter and desire them with greater desire. But the disbelievers share them with them, so that this distinction would not compel them to faith.

When this meaning is removed, they become exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection. If they were forbidden to the believers, they would have been created for the disbelievers, which contradicts the requirement of wisdom. If they were created for the believers, then the best time to benefit from them is when they proceed in accordance with faith, which is worship and piety, but without indulgence in desires.

﴿Thus We detail the signs for a people who know﴾: that is, the wisdom in creating things and using things in a way that benefits and does not harm. If they claim that one fears pride and indulgence in desires from adornment and enjoyment, and therefore these are forbidden to people of worship...

The discussion of the words of His exalted saying:

[33] ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, whether apparent or concealed, and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know.﴾

﴿Say﴾ "They are, in themselves, pure benefits." Their being a means to something else is a possibility that is not certain. So if it does lead to something, what is forbidden is that to which it leads, in itself, because ﴿My Lord has only forbidden indecencies﴾ "that is, those sins whose ugliness is extreme, that is, which have increased (and these are the major sins), and which are related to the private parts" ﴿whether apparent or concealed﴾ "that is, what some of them openly do to one another, and what some of them hide from others, and what appears of the actions of the limbs, and what is concealed of the actions of the hearts." ﴿And sin﴾ "that is, what makes one liable to sin, and it is general for every sin; He mentioned it for generalization after specification. It is said that sin (ithm) is wine. The poet said:

"The Messenger of Allah forbade us to approach fornication, and to drink the sin which brings about burden."

Al-Akhfash recited:

"I drank sin until my reason went astray *** Likewise, sin takes away the intellects."

This is transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan, and the lexicographers such as al-Asma'i and others mentioned it. Al-Hasan said: "His saying confirms it: ﴿In them is great sin﴾ [al-Baqarah: 219]."

Ibn al-Anbari said: "The Arabs did not call wine sin (ithm) in the Jahiliyyah or in Islam, and the poem cited is fabricated." It was answered that it is a metonymy, because it is its cause. Abu Hayyan said: "This explanation is not correct here, because the surah is Meccan, and wine was not prohibited except in Medina after Uhud, and others preceded him to this."

Also, restriction (hasr) requires evidence; so says al-Inayah.

﴿And oppression﴾ "that is, domineering over people and wronging them. He singled it out for mention, although it is included in what precedes it, to emphasize the warning against it. That is because singling it out for mention indicates that it is distinguished from among them until it is counted as an independent category." ﴿Without right﴾ "is connected to (oppression), emphasizing its meaning. It was said: oppression may cease to be wrongdoing if it is for a cause permitted in the Sharia, such as retaliation (qisas), but such a thing is not called oppression in its literal sense, rather by figurative association (mushakalah)." And "He has forbidden" that you associate with Allah that "for which He has sent down no authority" "that is, proof, that is, that for which no argument has been established."

Al-Zamakhshari said: "In it is mockery, because it is not possible that He send down proof for associating anything else with Him."

In al-Inayah: "The mockery arises from the fact that it implies that if there were authority for it, it would not be forbidden, indicating their imitation (taqlid) in error; and the meaning is negating both the sending down and the authority together, in the most eloquent manner." End.

Al-Razi said: "This verse is among the strongest proofs that the view of taqlid is false." Al-Qadi followed him and said: "In the verse is a warning against forbidding the following of what is not indicated by proof." And "He has forbidden you" that you "say about Allah what you do not know" "that is, that you fabricate about Him, and invent lies regarding permitting and forbidding, or regarding association."

Note of caution:

Al-Jashami said: The verse indicates the prohibition of all sins, because His saying "indecencies and sin" includes the minor and the major, the ugly deeds, the contracts contrary to the Sharia, the false statements, and the false beliefs.

Included in His saying ﴿whether apparent or concealed﴾ are the actions of the limbs, the actions of the hearts, (p-2675) treacheries, deceit and trickery. Included under His saying ﴿and oppression﴾ is every injustice that transgresses against others, including what rebels and Kharijites do, and rulers who gain victory without right. Included under His saying ﴿and that you associate﴾ is the prohibition of every association and worship directed to other than Allah. Included under His saying ﴿and that you say﴾ is every innovation, every error, every fatwa without right, and false testimony and the like.

So the verse is comprehensive regarding what is forbidden, just as what precedes it is comprehensive regarding what is permitted, and it contains instruction in manners, religious and worldly, and indicates the invalidity of taqlid, because it obligates following proof, by His saying ﴿for which He has sent down no authority﴾, and authority means proof.

It also indicates that every person has a time of life and a time of death, in which there is no advancing or delaying, so the saying of one who says "the one killed died before his appointed term" is invalid. End.

Then the Exalted warned the people of Makkah of a punishment descending at a known term with Him, glorified be He, as it descended upon the nations. So He, exalted, said:

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 7, verse 34:

The discussion of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[34] ﴿And for every nation there is a term. So when their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it.﴾

﴿And for every nation there is a term﴾ — i.e., a period or a time for the descent of the punishment upon them. ﴿So when their term comes﴾ — i.e., their appointed time decreed for them. ﴿They cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it﴾ — i.e., they will not be left a little while beyond the term, nor will they be destroyed before it. The "hour" is a figure of speech for the utmost smallness of time.

Subtleties:

1. This construction occurs in one place in the Revelation, and there is a well-known discussion concerning it. Since the apparent reading is that "nor can they advance it" (لا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ) is coordinated with "they cannot delay it" (لا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ), as al-Hawfi and others parsed it, it has been objected that this is invalid, because "idha" (إذا, "when") is only followed by future matters, not past ones. Advancing, in that case, relative to the place of the term is prior to it, so how can what precedes it be consequent upon it? This would turn the statement into a stating of the self-evident with no benefit, like your saying: "If I stand up in the future, your standing did not precede in the past."

It has been answered that the intended sense of "coming" is approaching, to the extent that advancing is possible in some respect, like the coming of the day for which an hour was set for their destruction within it.

It has been said that the clause "nor can they advance it" is a new, independent sentence. It has been said that it is coordinated to the condition and its answer, or to the restriction and the restricted, or that the whole of "they cannot delay it... nor can they advance it" is a metaphor (kinaya) for their inability to change it.

The verified view is that it is coordinated to "they cannot delay it" (يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ), but not to show the negation of advancing while advancing is possible in itself, as with delaying, as is supposed. Rather, it is for emphasis in negating delay, meaning that delay is equal to advance in impossibility. For this reason He arranged it together with it in one thread, as in His, the Glorified's, saying: ﴿And repentance is not for those who commit evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now," nor for those who die while they are disbelievers﴾ [An-Nisa: 18]. For whoever dies a disbeliever, while it is clear that there is no repentance for him at all, has been arranged in non-acceptance in the same thread as one who postponed it until death was present, signaling that the existence of repentance at that time and its non-existence are equal absolutely.

2. The mention of the negation of delay is placed first because the primary intent is to show that they cannot escape the punishment. As for "ma" (ما) in His saying: ﴿No nation can precede its term, nor can they delay﴾ [Al-Hijr: 5], the precedence (السَّبْق) is mentioned first; since the purpose there is to explain the secret of delaying their destruction despite their deserving it, as His saying indicates: ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them; they will come to know﴾ [Al-Hijr: 3]. Therefore, the more important matter there is to explain the negation of precedence.

3. The form of the reflexive verb (istif'al, الاستفعال) indicates their incapacity and deprivation of that, along with their seeking it. Abu al-Su'ud stated this.

Then He, the Exalted, warned the children of Adam that He would send to them messengers who would guide them, and gave glad tidings and warning with His, the Glorified's, saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 7, verse 35:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[35] ﴿O children of Adam, if there come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses, then whoever fears God and makes amends, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve.﴾

"﴿O children of Adam, if there come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses﴾" The conditional here is introduced with the particle of doubt, to alert that the coming of messengers is a permissible matter, not a necessary one. "Mā" has been appended to it to emphasize the meaning of the condition, and for this reason its verb is emphasized with the heavy or light nun. By "the children of Adam" is meant all the nations, and it is a narration of what occurred with every people. The intended "messengers" are not our Prophet ﷺ, and "the children of Adam" are not his community, as has been said, for that contradicts the apparent meaning; so reported in (al-Qadi) and its glosses. The answer to the condition is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿whoever fears God﴾, that is, denies [the messengers], ﴿and makes amends﴾, that is, his deeds, ﴿there will be no fear for them﴾, that is, of punishment, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾, that is, in the Hereafter.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted be He:**

[36] ﴿Those who denied Our signs and were arrogant towards them, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾

"﴿Those who denied Our signs and were arrogant﴾" meaning they became proud ﴿towards them﴾," so they did not believe in them. ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾

**Admonition:**

al-Jushami (al-Jushamī) said: The verse indicates the obligation to follow the Messengers and to accept what they convey. It also indicates that the good in Messengers is that they be among the people to whom they were sent, because they are better acquainted with their way, further from aversion to them, and closer to being at ease with them. It also indicates that the purpose of the Messenger is what he conveys of the proofs; therefore we said that it is not permissible for anyone to be a Messenger unless he has with him what he conveys. It also indicates that Paradise is attained by two things: (p-2678) good deeds and avoiding sins. Thus the saying of the Murji'ah (those who deferred judgment on the believer's works, holding that faith is not affected by deeds) is invalidated.

It also indicates that the believer in the Hereafter neither fears nor grieves, contrary to what the Ahsadiyyah (sic) and the Hashwiyyah (literalist anthropomorphists) say; so said most of our companions.

Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ali (al-Jassas) said: His saying ﴿so no fear will be upon them﴾ [al-A'raf: 35] is like the saying of the physician to the patient, "There is no harm upon you," meaning that his affair will end in well-being. But this is not the correct view, because it negates fear and grief absolutely. It also indicates the threat against the deniers, just as it indicates the promise to the obedient, as encouragement and warning. It also indicates that piety, righteousness, and denial are the act of the servant, thereby invalidating their saying regarding createdness (of acts) and capacity (istita'ah). The end of his words, may God have mercy on him.

Then, exalted is He, mentioned the threat against the deniers mentioned earlier, with His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion of the words of God, Exalted is He:

[37] ﴿Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His verses? Those will receive their share of what is decreed for them from the Book, until when Our messengers come to them to take their souls, they say: "Where is that which you used to invoke besides Allah?" They say: "They have gone astray from us," and they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers.﴾

"﴿Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His verses?﴾ That is: who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah concerning the lawful and the unlawful, or by attributing a son or a partner to Him, or who denies His revealed verses. ﴿Those will receive their share of what is decreed for them from the Book﴾ That is: their portion of what has been written for them of provision and lifespan and other things reaches them. That is, despite their wrongdoing, their fabrication and their denial, they are not deprived of what has been decreed for them of lifespan and provision until the end of their appointed terms.

There are other interpretations of the verse. This one is the clearest and strongest in meaning, and the continuation of the verse points to it, and in this case it accords with its parallels, such as the words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah will not succeed﴾ [Yunus: 69] ﴿A brief enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾ [Yunus: 70].

And His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ [Luqman: 23] ﴿We will give them enjoyment for a little﴾ [Luqman: 24], to the end of the verse. ﴿Until when Our messengers come to them to take their souls﴾ That is: the angels of death seize their souls. ﴿They say: "Where is that which you used to invoke besides Allah?"﴾ That is: where are the deities you used to worship so that they would be intercessors for you? We do not see them rescuing you from these hardships that have befallen you.

The question serves two purposes: a rebuke and reproach to them, which increases their grief upon grief, and a kindness toward the accountable person, for when he conceives of this, it turns him away from denial. The "mā" was written joined to "ayna" in the ʿUthmanic codex (rasm al-muṣḥaf), while the rule of convention requires separation, since it is a relative (mawṣūlah). ﴿They say: "They have gone astray from us"﴾ That is: they vanished from us, so they did not rescue us from anything. ﴿And they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers﴾ That is: worshippers of what does not deserve worship. They acknowledged that they were not upon anything in what they had been upon, and that they did not praise Him in the end."

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[38] ﴿He said: Enter among nations that have passed away before you, of jinn and humankind, into the Fire. Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister, until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say of the first of them: "Our Lord, these are the ones who led us astray, so give them a double punishment of the Fire." He will say: "For each there is double, but you do not know."﴾

﴿He said﴾: That is, God, glorified is He, says to them in the Hereafter. ﴿Enter among nations that have passed away﴾: that is, among the host of nations that have gone before. ﴿before you, of jinn and humankind﴾: meaning the disbelievers of the past nations of both kinds. ﴿into the Fire﴾: this is connected to "enter". ﴿Every time a nation enters﴾: that is, into the Fire. ﴿it curses its sister﴾: that is, the one before it, because of its having led it astray, as the Friend (al-Khalil), upon him be prayer and peace, said: ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection some of you will disown others﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 25], and so on.

﴿until, when they have all overtaken one another therein﴾: that is, "tada rakū" (تدارَكوا), meaning they follow one another closely and gather together in the Fire. ﴿the last of them﴾: and they are the followers, ﴿will say of the first of them﴾: that is, on account of the first of them, since the address is to God, exalted is He, not to them. Ibn Kathir said: That is, the last of them in entering, who are the followers, will say about their predecessors, who are the leaders, because they were the greater in sin than their followers, and so they entered before them. The followers will complain of them to God on the Day of Resurrection, because they are the ones who led them astray from the right path. So they will say: ﴿Our Lord, these are the ones who led us astray﴾: that is, they set down misguidance for us and called to it, so we followed them. ﴿So give them a double punishment of the Fire﴾: that is, doubled, because they went astray and led others astray. ﴿He will say﴾: that is, God, exalted is He, ﴿For each there is double﴾: that is, a doubled punishment. As for the leaders and chiefs, it is for their going astray and leading astray; as for the followers and the lowly, it is for their going astray and their imitation of those who went astray, despite the presence of guides with decisive proofs. ﴿But you do not know﴾: that is, what is due to you, or what is due to each group. It is also read with the letter ya' (يَعْلَمُونَ), and on that reading it is a concluding remark (tadhyil) not intended to be included within the answer.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[39] ﴿And its first (group) will say to its last: "You had no superiority over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn."﴾

"﴿And its first (group) will say to its last: You had no superiority over us﴾ meaning: you have no advantage over us in abandoning disbelief and misguidance, so that our punishment would be doubled and yours would not. You have gone astray just as we have gone astray, so we and you are equal in misguidance and in deserving the punishment. As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿so taste the punishment for what you used to earn﴾, it is either the words of the leaders, or the words of God, exalted is He, to both groups, and this is the more apparent."

(p-٢٦٨١)Remark:

Al-Jashami said: The verse indicates that the disbelievers, the misguided and the innovators (al-mubtadi'ah), even if they support one another and cooperate in their misguidance and show affection for one another in this world, will in the Hereafter curse one another, cut off from one another, and ask for punishment for those who led them astray. It also indicates the corruption of taqlid (blind imitation, following without evidence), and of being deceived by the words of evil scholars. It indicates that the one who calls to misguidance is a misleader. It indicates that another's leading one astray is not an excuse for him. It also indicates that their sharing in the punishment does not bring them any relief, unlike sharing in the trials of this world. And it indicates that this leading astray was their own act, which invalidates the claim of the Mujbirah (the determinists, who hold that man is compelled) regarding the creature, and regarding guidance and misguidance.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 7, verse 40:

The interpretation of His statement, exalted is He:

[40] ﴿Indeed, those who deny Our signs and act arrogantly toward them – for them the gates of heaven will not be opened, nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. And thus do We recompense the criminals.﴾

"﴿Indeed, those who deny Our signs and act arrogantly toward them – for them the gates of heaven will not be opened﴾: that is, their deeds will not be lifted up, nor their supplication, nor anything by which they seek obedience to God. That is, it will not be accepted from them, because it is neither righteous nor good. And He, glorified is He, has said: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it﴾ [Fatir: 10]. Ibn 'Abbas said: That is, no righteous deed or supplication of theirs will be raised up to Him from it, as related by a group from him. And Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr said the same.

Or the meaning is: blessing and mercy will not descend upon them, and they will not be given relief, because He has made it customary for mercy to descend from the sky, as in His statement: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water﴾ [al-Qamar: 11].

Or the meaning is: they will not be permitted to ascend to heaven, nor will a path be opened for them to it so that they may enter Paradise, according to what is reported that Paradise is in the sky.

Or the meaning is: the gates of heaven will not be opened for their souls when they die, as they are opened for the souls of the believers. This was related by al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Jarir related from al-Bara' that the Messenger of God ﷺ mentioned the taking of the soul of the wicked person, and that it is carried up to heaven, and they ascend with it, and they do not pass by any assembly of angels without them saying: "What is this foul spirit?" And they say: "So-and-so!" (with the worst of the names by which he was called in the world), until they reach with it the sky, and they ask for it to be opened, but it is not opened for him. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ recited: ﴿The gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾, the verse.

Ibn Kathir said: Thus he related it. It is a portion of a long hadith, which Imam Ahmad related at length, and Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah related through several chains.

(p-2683) Remarks:

The first: al-Shihab said: That the heaven has gates, and that it is opened for the good supplication, and for the ascending deeds, or for the souls, is stated in the Qur'anic texts and the prophetic hadiths, so there is no need for interpretation. End of quote.

(p-2684) This is according to the principle of the Literalists (ahl al-zahir) in such matters, except that the application is not restricted to the literal sense. The noble Revelation came in the various modes of expression known to the Arabs in their speech. And God knows best.

(p-2685) The second: the doubling in (tufattahu) is for multiplying the object, not the action, since the context does not fit it.

The third: it was read with a single letter in (tufatahu), and with the single letter and the ya', and it was read in the active voice with the accusative (al-abwab), on the basis that the action is attributed to the verses metaphorically, and with the ya' on the basis that it is attributed to God, exalted is He.

﴿And they will not enter Paradise until he passes﴾, that is, enters, ﴿the camel into the eye of the needle﴾: that is, the hole of the needle, and that is impossible, so their entry is likewise impossible.

Subtleties:

The first: The majority read (al-jamal) with a fatha on the jim and the mim, and they explained it as the well-known camel, the beast of burden. Al-Farra' said: al-jamal is the mate of the she-camel. Shamir said: al-bikr and al-bikrah stand in the same relation as the boy and the girl, and al-jamal and al-naqah as the man and the woman. It was read in the anomalous readings as (al-jummal), like sukkar, surad and qufl, and 'unuq and jabl, meaning the thick rope of a ship, which is called (al-qals).

Abu al-Baqa' said: It is read in the anomalous reading with the mim sukun, and the better view is that it is a dialect form, because lightening a fatha is weak; and it is read with a damma on the jim and fatha on the mim with shaddah, and it is the thick rope, and it is a plural like sawwam and qawwam; and it is read with damma on the jim and mim with lightening, and it is a plural like asad and usud; and it is read likewise except that the mim is sakin, and that is on the lightening of the damma. End of quote.

al-Kawashi mentioned that the readings mentioned are all dialects for the camel, apart from (jumallan) like sukkar and qufl, and this was disputed. End of quote.

Its reading as (sukkar), in the sense of the rope mentioned, was related by Mujahid and 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr preferred it.

al-Zamakhshari said: And from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that God is too exalted in His comparison to compare to the camel; the rope is suitable for the thread that passes through the eye of the needle, while the camel is not suitable for it. However, the reading of the common people is more fitting, because the eye of the needle is a proverb for narrowness of passage; it is said: "narrower than the hole of the needle."

(p-2686) They also called the skilled guide (khirrit) for beginning with him in narrow places likened to the points of needles, and the camel is a proverb for massiveness of body. He said:

*The body of camels and the dreams of sparrows*

The men are not like a slaughtered beast whose bodies are wanted, so it was said: they will not enter Paradise until there occurs what never occurs ever, the passage of this animal which passes only through a wide door, and through the eye of a needle. And from Ibn Mas'ud: that he was asked about the camel, and he said: "the mate of the she-camel," mocking the questioner, and indicating that seeking another meaning is affectation. End of quote.

The summary is that since the camel is a proverb for massiveness of body, for it is the largest of animals in body among the Arabs, and the eye of a needle is a proverb for narrowness, the correspondence appears. Moreover, in preferring the camel, which is not by nature suited to passing through the eye of a needle, there is an exaggeration in deeming their entry into Paradise improbable.

The second: al-samm: the narrow hole. Abu al-Baqa' said: with a fatha and a damma on the sin, two dialects. End of quote.

The triple vocalisation in it, and in the well-known word for poison, was stated by the author of al-Qamus and others, except that they said: the more well-known for the hole is the fatha, as in the revelation, and the more eloquent for the poison is the damma.

al-'Allama al-Fasi said: al-Zabidi said: I have not seen anyone address its kasra, and it seems to be colloquial.

I say: al-Zamakhshari said: And it was read ﴿fi samm al-khiyat﴾ with the three vowels, and that suffices as a reference.

The third: (al-khiyat) like kitab and minbar is what the garment is sewn with, and the needle, as in al-Qamus.

al-Zamakhshari said: 'Abdullah read (fi samm al-makhit). al-Shihab said: with a kasra and a fatha on the mim, as the grammarian mentioned, and it is an anomalous reading.

The fourth: al-Suyuti said in (al-Iklil): In His statement, exalted is He: ﴿until the camel passes﴾ etc., the permissibility of assuming the impossible, and making a conditional upon it, as often occurs for jurists. End of quote.

The making of a conditional upon the impossible is well known in Arabic speech, as in his saying:

*When the crow grows white, I shall come to my family, and pitch becomes like milk, fresh*

And His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And thus﴾, that is, like that dreadful recompense, ﴿do We recompense the criminals﴾.

Commentary on the Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[41] ﴿For them there will be a bed of Hell, and above them coverings. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿For them there will be a bed of Hell﴾ — i.e., a bedding beneath them. ﴿And above them coverings﴾ — i.e., covers, when sin encompasses them. ﴿Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ — i.e., with disbelief. He referred to them at one point as "the criminals" (al-mujrimun) and at another as "the wrongdoers" (al-zalimun), to indicate that by their denial of the signs, they were characterized by each of these two ugly attributes.
