He, exalted is He, represented their creation upon the innate disposition of monotheism (fiṭrat al-tawḥīd), and their being brought out from the loins of their fathers, as witnesses to His lordship with a testimony free of doubt, by His making them acknowledge it through a command, and their prompt hastening to that without any hesitation whatsoever. The purpose of the verse is to argue against the polytheists by their knowledge of His lordship, exalted is He, a knowledge of the innate disposition (fiṭrī), inherent in them with the inevitability of confession and testimony. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fiṭrah of God upon which He has created mankind. No change should there be in the creation of God.﴾ [al-Rūm: 30]. The fiṭrah (innate disposition) is the knowledge of His lordship.

[p-2898] In the Two Ṣaḥīḥs (al-Ṣaḥīḥayn, Bukhari and Muslim) from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No child is born except upon the fiṭrah. Then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete animal. Do you see any mutilation in it?"

al-Jamāʾ is the one whose ear is intact, and al-Jadʿāʾ is the one whose ear is cut off.

In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God says: Indeed I created My servants as ḥunafāʾ (upright in faith), then the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them."

Al-Ṭabarī narrated from al-Ḥasan, from al-Aswad ibn Sarīʿ, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Every soul (nasamah) is born upon the fiṭrah until its tongue expresses it, and then its parents make it a Jew or a Christian." Al-Ḥasan said: "By God, God has indeed said in His Book: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾..." the verse. This was narrated by Imam Aḥmad and al-Nasāʾī, without al-Ḥasan's citing of the verse.

As for the reports transmitted concerning the bringing forth of the offspring from the loins of Adam (peace be upon him), God's speaking to them and their speaking, then His returning them to their father's loins, these are not sound in their chains of transmission. As for those whose chains are sound, they are not explicit on this, but rather are closer to the wording of the verse, as Ḥāfiẓ (the memorizer) Ibn Kathīr made clear. He, may God have mercy on him, said: For this reason, some of the early generations (al-salaf) and later generations (al-khalaf) said that what is meant by this "making them testify" is that He created them upon monotheism, as has preceded in the hadiths of Abu Hurayrah, ʿIyāḍ and al-Aswad. Al-Ḥasan also explained the verse in this way.

They said: The meaning of "He made them testify" (ashhadahum) is that He brought them into existence as witnesses to that, speaking to Him by state and by word. Testimony (shahādah) is sometimes by word, as in His saying: ﴿They will say: We testify against ourselves﴾ [al-Anʿām: 130], and sometimes by state, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God while testifying against themselves of disbelief﴾ [al-Tawbah: 17], meaning their state is a witness against them of that, because they are, by their state, saying that. Likewise His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, he is a witness to that﴾ [al-ʿĀdiyāt: 7]. Just as a request (suʾāl) is sometimes by word (qāl) and sometimes by state (ḥāl), as in His saying: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 34].

They said: Among what indicates that this is the meaning is that He made the testimony a proof against them regarding polytheism. If this had happened as the one who said it claims, then everyone would remember it, so that it would be a proof against him. If it is said: The Messenger's (ﷺ) report of it is sufficient for its existence. The answer is that the polytheist deniers reject everything the messengers brought them concerning this and other things, while this was made an independent proof against them. This shows that it is the fiṭrah upon which they were created, the acknowledgment of monotheism.

﴿An taqūlū﴾ means: lest you say, out of dislike, ﴿yawm al-qiyāmah﴾ ("on the Day of Resurrection"), that is, the day on which one is questioned about lordship and monotheism. ﴿Innā kunnā ʿan hādhā﴾ means: "Indeed we were, concerning this," that is, concerning His lordship and His oneness, ﴿ghāfilīn﴾ ("unaware"), that is, we were not alerted to it.

For since they were created with what has been mentioned, they become without excuse, unable to offer this as a plea, since no one has any way to deny what has been mentioned of their creation upon the sound fiṭrah.

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[173] ﴿Or lest you say: "It was only our fathers who associated partners with God before, and we were offspring after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾

"﴿Or lest you say: It was only our fathers who associated partners with God﴾" i.e., they initiated (sanna) association and invented it. "﴿before﴾" i.e., before our time. "﴿and we were offspring after them﴾" i.e., we grew up following their way, arguing by imitation (taqlid) and relying upon it. Thus We have cut off the excuse by what We have made clear of the signs. "﴿Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?﴾" i.e., will You punish us for the shirk that our fathers committed, and which they founded upon falsehood; or for the deeds of our fathers who nullified the influence of reason and the words of the Messengers? The interrogation is one of denial, meaning: You are Wise, and You do not hold the sons to account for the deeds of the fathers, especially when we have followed their path, and the proof against them is what they legislated for us of falsehood. The meaning: We have removed the two doubts, namely that acknowledgment of Lordship and monotheism lies in the origin of your nature (fitrah); so why did you not return to it when reason and the Messengers called you? The fitrah is the greatest proof; it closes the door of excuse in every respect, especially since imitation, when the proofs are established and the capacity to reason by them exists, has no basis at all.

Admonitions:

The first: Imam Ibn Kathir, in this place too, agreed with al-Jashmi (al-Jushami) in his tafsir. He said: The people of hadith narrate from their predecessors, by way of transmitted reports both mawquf and marfu', and make that the interpretation of the verse: that He wiped the back of Adam, brought forth from it his offspring like specks (adh-dharr), and said: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes, we bear witness," in obedience, then He returned them into the loins of Adam. And the interpretation of the verse is according to that.

He said: Our teachers, may God have mercy on them, have mentioned that this is corrupt, that the apparent meaning of the verse contradicts it, and they mentioned in the report what we shall mention. They said: Among what proves its corruption are several points.

Among them: if the matter were as they mentioned, we would have been told of it, for such a great event would not be forgotten by any reasonable person, especially if they were made to bear witness to it so that they would act by it.

Among them: what our shaykh Abu 'Ali mentioned, that the back of Adam cannot contain this great multitude, and this is a monstrous statement.

Among them: that He mentioned that He created us from a drop (nutfah), and every child is born of a father and of a drop; so if He created them at the beginning from nothing, this would not be valid.

Among them: that a single part cannot be living and rational, because that structure does not bear life, so it must be composed of parts, and then it is not valid that all of them be in the back of Adam.

(p-2901) Among them: that it opens the door to metempsychosis (tanasukh) and the doctrine of return, for they could say: if re-creation is possible there, then it does not deny transmigration.

Among them: that it must have a benefit, and its benefit would be that He mention it so that they proceed according to that method; and if He does not mention it, its benefit is void.

Among them: that acknowledgment is not valid unless there has previously been a state in which they knew this; so how is it valid at the beginning of creation, and other points that reason does not accept.

Then he said: Our teachers, may God have mercy on them, said: The apparent meaning of the verse is contrary to their view in several respects:

Among them: He said: "﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾" [al-A'raf: 172], and did not say "from Adam." And He said "from their backs" and did not say "from his back," and He said "﴿their offspring﴾" [al-A'raf: 172] and did not say "his offspring."

Among them: He said: "﴿lest you say﴾" [al-A'raf: 172], meaning the doing of that, so that you do not say: "Indeed we were heedless of this." And what heedlessness is greater than that all the sensible do not recall anything of that?

Among them: He said: "﴿It was only our fathers who associated partners﴾" and there was not for them on that day any father who was a polytheist. All of this shows the corruption of what they say. None of our teachers authenticated this report or accepted it; rather they rejected it, except Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn 'Ali, who permitted it without asserting its soundness; but he said: That is not the interpretation of the verse, and he mentioned that the benefit of that is that they proceed upon the noble lineages in thanking the blessing and affirming Lordship, just as he said that they were born upon the fitrah; he said: He brought them forth like specks, then inspired them until they said "Yes." End of what al-Jashmi said.

The second: The verse indicates the corruption of blind imitation (taqlid) in religion, and indicates that God has removed the excuse and cleared away the pretext, and after that no one is excused. Mentioned by al-Jashmi.

The third: It has been argued from this verse and the hadiths preceding it in meaning that the knowledge of Him, Exalted, is innate (fitri) and necessary (daruri). God, Exalted, said: ﴿Their messengers said: Is there doubt about God?﴾ [Ibrahim: 10], and He, Exalted, said: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say: God﴾ [Luqman: 25]

﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 86] ﴿They will say: God. Say: Will you not then fear Him?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 87]

"It is narrated from Imran ibn Husayn who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to my father: 'O Husayn, how many gods do you worship today?' My father said: Seven, six on the earth and one in the heaven. He said: 'Which of them do you prepare for your desire and your fear?' He said: The one who is in the heaven." Related by at-Tirmidhi. So God, Exalted, created all creation upon the knowledge of Him, a fitrah of monotheism, even he who was created insane, completely afflicted, understanding nothing, who swears by none but Him, and whose tongue does not move with more than His holy name, a complete fitrah.

Shaykh al-Taqi Ibn Taymiyya said: The acknowledgment and recognition of the Creator is innate and necessary in the souls of people, though some people may have something occur that corrupts their fitrah, until they need a reflection by which knowledge is attained for them. This is the saying of the majority of people, and it is the view of the skilled theologians (nuzzar): that knowledge is attained by necessity, and it may be attained by reflection for one whose fitrah has been corrupted, as many of the imams of the mutakallimun have acknowledged.

He also said: Some theologians held that knowledge of God is obligatory and that there is no way to it except by reflection, so they made reflection obligatory upon everyone. This view became famous in the community specifically from the Mu'tazila and their like. Therefore Abu Ja'far al-Simnani and others said: The Ash'ari's making reflection obligatory in knowledge is a remnant that remained with him from Mu'tazilism.

He, may God have mercy on him, mentioned that what the words of the imams and the predecessors indicate—and it is the most just of the sayings—is that reflection is obligatory in one state and not in another, and upon one person and not another; so its obligation is among the accidental matters that are obligatory upon some people in some circumstances, not among the general necessary matters. Those who made reflection obligatory do not possess what indicates the general obligation of it; it only indicates that it may be obligatory, as in His saying: ﴿Say: Look at what is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [Yunus: 101] (p-2903) and His saying: ﴿So let man look at what he was created from﴾ [al-Tariq: 5], for it is an address to the arrogant deniers, who were commanded to look so that they might know the truth and acknowledge it; and there is no doubt that reflection is obligatory upon these.

Abu Hayyan al-Tawhidi said in his Muqabasat, in the forty-second muqabasa: It was said to Abu al-Khayr: "Tell us about the knowledge of God, may He be exalted: is it a necessity (darurah) or an inference (istidlal)? For the speakers on this have differed greatly and have opposed one another with great enmity, and we wish to have an answer which explains it briefly with clarity."

He said: It is a necessity from the side of the intellect, and an inference from the side of the senses. Since every knowable object is either sought by the intellect in the intelligible, or by the senses in the sensible, it is possible that one might at one time suppose that knowledge of Him is acquisition and inference, because the sensing person examines and is strengthened by the support and backing of the intellect and its attainment. And at another time one might suppose that it is a necessity, for the sound intellect, free from defect and clear of blemish, urges acknowledgment of God, may His name be holy, and forbids its possessor to deny Him, to disbelieve in Him, or to doubt Him; but it is a necessity fitting to the intellect, for the necessity of the intellect is not like the necessity of the senses, since the necessity of the senses involves pulling and choosing, and carrying and compulsion, whereas the necessity of the intellect is very gentle, for it admonishes, befriends, advises, and lightens.

Then he gave a subtle example, and after it said: On this basis, God, may His name be holy, is known to the intellect by necessity, with no doubt about His existence in it, and is inferred by the senses, for it is greatly subject to change and does not stand firm at all; so whoever infers ascends from particulars, and whoever claims necessity descends from universals.

Both paths have been clarified by this consideration, and one is spared the burden of stumbling and excess. As for what is investigated through dispute, it inherits from it nothing but doubt, division, fanaticism, and partisanship; there passpassion has its birth and nurture, falsehood has dominion and roaming, and bewilderment has stillness and residence. May God take us by our hands and spare us the passion that harms us. End.

And His, Exalted, saying:

(p-2904)The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[174] ﴿And thus do We detail the verses, so that perhaps they will return.﴾

"And thus do We detail the verses, so that perhaps they will return." That is, in the same manner as what we have mentioned, We make clear the proofs and arguments, so that they may return to the truth.

And His words, may He be exalted:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[175] ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them, so Satan followed him, and he became of the misguided.﴾

﴿And recite to them﴾: that is, to your people, or to the Jews.

﴿the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs﴾: that is, the knowledge of the Book. He was given gentle guidance until he learned and understood its meanings and became a scholar of them.

﴿but he detached himself from them﴾: by God withdrawing the knowledge from him, so that he disbelieved in them and came out of them the way a snake comes out of its skin.

﴿so Satan followed him﴾: that is, he caught up with him, overtook him, and became his companion until he led him astray.

﴿and he became of the misguided﴾

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 7, verse 176:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[176] ﴿And had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his desire. So his example is like the example of a dog: if you attack it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories, perhaps they will reflect.﴾

"﴿And had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby﴾": i.e., We would have exalted him by acting upon them.

"﴿But he clung to the earth﴾": i.e., he inclined toward this world and desired it.

"﴿And followed his desire. So his example is like the example of a dog: if you attack it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants﴾": This is because the bestowal of the signs, the obligation to act by them, the honour gained through them, and the lack of all this are equal in his case, like the dog that lolls its tongue in every state. "If you attack it" means: if you chase it and stir it up; "or leave it" means: if you leave it without provoking it by attack, its panting is present in both states alike. "That is the example of the people who denied Our signs": i.e., of the Torah or others. "So relate the stories, perhaps they will reflect."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 7, verse 177:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[177] ﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs and were wronging themselves.﴾

"﴿Evil is the example﴾" i.e., evil is that with which they are compared. "﴿The people who denied Our signs﴾" i.e., they are likened to dogs, either in that both states are equal in deficiency and that they are misguided, whether they were admonished or not, as we have already mentioned; or in baseness, for the dog has no aspiration except to obtain a morsel of food or an appetite. Whoever departs from the sphere of guidance and knowledge and turns toward his own desires becomes like the dog, and evil is the example of such a one. For this reason it is established in the Sahih from him (ﷺ) that he said: "We have no example of evil: the one who takes back his gift is like the dog that returns to its vomit."

"﴿And they were wronging themselves﴾" Know that among the early generations (al-salaf) there were those who held that this verse is an example God struck for one to whom faith was presented, but who refused to accept it and abandoned it. This is the view of Qatadah and Ikrimah, and Abu Muslim chose it, saying: His saying "﴿We gave him Our signs﴾" [al-A'raf: 175] means: We made them clear, but he did not accept them, and he stripped himself of them. The phrase "he withdrew from them" (insalakha), "he stripped himself" (a'ra), and "he distanced himself" (tabaa'ada) are equivalent in meaning, and this applies to every disbeliever who was not persuaded by the proofs and persisted in disbelief. He said: A parallel to it is His saying, exalted is He: "﴿O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you﴾" [an-Nisa': 47], and He said concerning Pharaoh: "﴿And We had shown him all Our signs, but he denied and refused﴾" [Ta-Ha: 56].

Among them are those who held that the relative pronoun in it refers to a specific person. It is related from Abdullah ibn Umar, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Zayd ibn Aslam and Abu Rawq that he was Umayyah ibn Abi as-Salt, for he had read the scriptures and knew that God was sending a messenger at that time, and he hoped that he would be that messenger. When God sent Muhammad (peace be upon him), he envied him, then died a disbeliever and did not believe in the Prophet (ﷺ). It is he about whom the Messenger of God said: "Indeed, his poetry believed, but his heart disbelieved," meaning that his poetry was like the poetry of the believers, for he affirmed the oneness of God in his poetry and mentioned the proofs of His oneness.

It was also said: It was revealed concerning Abu Amir the monk, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) named "the Wicked." He used to practise monasticism in the Jahiliyyah, and when Islam came he went out to Syria, and he commanded the hypocrites to build the mosque of harm and division, and he went to Caesar and sought his help against the Prophet (ﷺ), and he died there, an exile and alone. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.

It was also said that it was revealed concerning the hypocrites among the People of the Book, who knew the Prophet (ﷺ) but denied him. This is related from al-Hasan and al-Asamm.

It was also said: it refers to Pharaoh, and the signs are the signs of Musa, as if, after relating the account of the Children of Israel, He returned to the story of Pharaoh and an example was struck for him.

Among the sayings that the exegetes have passed down is that it was revealed concerning Balam ibn Ba'ur, and they recount a story about him that is not transmitted in the major collections of authentic reports in our possession, nor does it agree with what the People of the Book have; his account is mentioned in the twenty-second and twenty-third chapters of the Book of Numbers, in the history of the Torah, in a manner different from what the exegetes relate about him. Then I saw that al-Jashami did not authenticate that, so I praised the Lord for the agreement. His words are: (It is related from Mujahid that he said: he is a prophet called Bal'um, whom his people bribed, so he disbelieved. This is not permissible, because disbelief cannot be attributed to the prophets, for that would repel people from the prophets and from accepting from them, and would belittle them in souls, and because they are the proofs of God over His creation whom He chose. So the closer view is that this is not authentically reported from Mujahid. End of quote.) And so it is, for whoever reads his account in the aforementioned Book sees, from his steadfastness and his not agreeing with Balak, king of Moab, to what he wanted from him, what clears him of that.

Note:

Al-Jashami said: If it is asked, how does the verse connect with what precedes it? We say: according to the view that it refers to Pharaoh, his story is connected with the story of the Children of Israel. It was also said: when He forbade blind imitation of the fathers in religion, He explained in this verse the condition of the scholars of evil, who prefer this world over the Hereafter, forbidding following and imitating them just as He forbade imitating the fathers. It was also said: when the mention of the taking of the covenant had preceded, He explained the condition of one whom God gave the signs, but who stripped himself of them and did not follow them. End.

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[178] ﴿Whomever Allah guides, he is the one guided; and whomever He leads astray, those are the losers.﴾

"Whomever Allah guides, he is the one guided; and whomever He leads astray, those are the losers." Abu al-Su'ud said: When He commanded the Prophet (ﷺ) to recount the account of the one who cast off (his signs) to these misguided people, whose likeness is his likeness, so that they would reflect upon it, abandon their inclination toward error, and be guided (ihtida') to the truth, He followed that with establishing that guidance (hidayah) and misguidance are from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Admonition and reminder are only among the customary means for attaining guidance, having no effect on it themselves, other than being motives that turn the servant's choice toward attaining it, in accordance with what Allah the Exalted has attached to it of His creation, like the rest of the actions of the servants.

[p. 2908]

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[179] ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, and they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. Those are the heedless.﴾

"﴿And We have certainly created﴾ i.e., We created." "﴿for Hell﴾ i.e., for its entry and for being punished therein." "﴿many of the jinn and mankind﴾, namely the disbelievers from both groups, who are described by His saying, exalted is He," "﴿they have hearts with which they do not understand﴾ i.e., the signs of God that guide to perfections." "﴿and they have eyes with which they do not see﴾ i.e., the proofs of His oneness, with the sight of reflection." "﴿and they have ears with which they do not hear﴾ i.e., the signs and admonitions, with the hearing of contemplation and receiving admonition. This means that they do not benefit from any of these faculties which God made a means of guidance, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And We made for them hearing and sight and hearts, but their hearing did not avail them, nor their sight, nor their hearts, in anything, since they had been rejecting the signs of God﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 26]." "﴿Those are like livestock﴾ i.e., the grazing animals, which do not benefit from these senses except in what sustains them, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the example of those who disbelieve is like one who shouts to that which hears nothing but a call and cry﴾ [al-Baqarah: 171], i.e., their example, in the state of being called to faith, is like the example of livestock when their shepherd calls them: they hear only his voice and do not understand what he says."

And His saying, exalted is He: "﴿Rather, they are more astray﴾ i.e., than the livestock, since the livestock do not have the capacity to attain those perfections and to remove those deficiencies. Yet they, despite possessing that capacity, have been empty of perfections and of removing their opposites, so they were worse in state than the livestock, because of their deficiency while the capacity for perfection exists within them. Also: the livestock perceive their benefits and harms, so they keep to some of what they perceive, whereas most of these people know that the truth is clear and yet they are obstinate, and they proceed into the Fire.

Also: the livestock may respond to their shepherd even though they do not understand his speech, unlike these people. Also: they do what they were created for, either by their nature or by being subjected to it, unlike these people, for they were created to worship God and to affirm His oneness, (p. 2909) but they disbelieved in Him and associated others with Him." "﴿Those are the heedless﴾ i.e., heedless of those perfections and deficiencies, so that they would be concerned to attain them and to remove them, as they are concerned with drawing worldly benefits and warding off their harms."

Note:

Abu al-Su'ud said: What is meant by these people who were created for Hell are those upon whom the eternal Word has been decreed with wretchedness, but not by way of compulsion, and not because of anything on their part that leads to it. Rather, because of His knowledge, exalted is He, that they will never turn their choice toward the truth, but will persist in falsehood without any turner to redirect them or any inclination to bend them from the signs and warnings. In this sense, their creation was made conditional upon it (Hell), just as for both groups, in view of their complete natural readiness for worship and their full capacity for it, their creation was made conditional upon worship. As His saying, exalted is He, expresses: ﴿I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56], and His saying, exalted is He—

The Interpretation of His, the Exalted, Words:

[180] ﴿To God belong the Most Beautiful Names, so call upon Him by them, and leave those who deviate concerning His Names. They will be recompensed for what they used to do.﴾

"﴿To God belong the Most Beautiful Names.﴾ Muqatil narrated that a man invoked God in his prayer, calling upon "al-Rahman" (the Most Merciful). Some of the polytheists said: "Muhammad and his companions claim that they worship one Lord, so why does this man call upon two?" Then the verse was revealed.

And "al-Husna" (the most beautiful) is the feminine form of "al-Ahsan" (the most excellent). The meaning is: to God belong the names that are the most excellent and most sublime, because they indicate the most excellent and noblest meanings. ﴿So call upon Him by them, and leave those who deviate concerning His Names﴾, meaning those who incline away from acknowledging them and deny them, and turn away from them in disbelief in them. Like His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿When it is said to them, "Prostrate yourselves to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate to whatever you command us?" And it increases them in aversion﴾ [al-Furqan: 60], meaning the mention of the Most Merciful increased them in aversion. For this reason He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: "Call upon God or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names"﴾ [al-Isra': 110]. And His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿They will be recompensed for what they used to do﴾ means in the Hereafter, for their denial of them and their aversion from believing in them.

Remarks:

First: Al-Sayyid Muhammad ibn al-Murtada al-Yamani said in (Iythar al-Haqq): The station of knowing the perfection of this Generous Lord, and what is due to Him of His attributes and His Most Beautiful Names, is part of complete monotheism, which is indispensable, because the perfection of the Essence is through its Beautiful Names and its noble attributes, and there is no perfection for an essence that has no attribute and no name.

For this reason, the doctrine of the heretics (al-malahidah) in denying them while praising the Lord is considered among their greatest schemes against Islam, for they reversed what is known by reason and revelation: they disparaged what is praiseworthy and praised what is blameworthy, which stands in place of pure negation and denial, and they opposed the Book of God and its clear texts.

God, majestic is His majesty, said: ﴿To God belong the Most Beautiful Names﴾, the verse. And He said: ﴿Say: "Call upon God or call upon the Most Merciful"﴾ [al-Isra': 110], the verse. Whatever of them is explicitly stated in the Book of God must be believed in by all, and whoever denies it, or claims that its apparent meaning is a name of blame for God, Glorified is He, is to be rebuked. Whatever is in a hadith, it is obligatory to believe in it for whoever knows its authenticity; whatever is below this rank, or whose authenticity is disputed, its use is not valid, for God is too exalted to be named by a name whose being a name of His has not been established. End.

Second: Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed God has ninety-nine names, whoever memorizes them enters Paradise, and God is Witr (One) and loves the witr." In another narration: "Whoever counts them." Al-Bukhari said: "We memorized it" is the meaning of "ahsaynahu" (we counted it). Al-Tirmidhi also transmitted it, and added the enumeration of the names, then said: "We do not know the names mentioned in most of the narrations except in this hadith." It was also transmitted by Ibn Majah, who listed the names with additions and omissions.

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: What a group of the memorizers relied upon is that the listing of the names in this hadith is an insertion (mudraj) into it, and that it is as narrated by al-Walid ibn Muslim and Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad al-San'ani, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, that it reached him from more than one of the people of knowledge that they said this, meaning that they collected them from the Qur'an, as was narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah and Abu Zayd al-Lughawi. End.

Al-Nawawi said: The scholars agree that this hadith does not contain a restriction of His, the Glorified and Exalted, names to these. Its meaning is not that He has no names other than these ninety-nine; rather, the intended purpose of the hadith is to inform about entering Paradise by counting them, not to inform about their being limited. For this reason another hadith came: "I ask You by every name You named Yourself with, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept hidden in the knowledge of the unseen with You." Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ibn al-Arabi al-Maliki mentioned from some of them that God has a thousand names. End.

Al-Sayyid al-Yamani said in (Iythar al-Haqq): It is the custom of the theologians here to limit themselves to a few of the names, and it is not appropriate to omit any of them or abridge them, for that is like abridging the Noble Qur'an. Had any of them been something one should not believe in or mention, God would not have mentioned it in the Mighty Qur'an.

It is the custom of some hadith scholars to cite everything that occurred in the famous hadith in enumerating them, despite the famous dispute over its authenticity. It suffices you that al-Bukhari and Muslim left its takhrij (transmission) aside, together with the narration of its beginning. Their agreement on that indicates the strength of the defect in it. But most scholars relied on it, seeking the great favor of God in His promise to whoever counts them with Paradise, as its authenticity is agreed upon. The counting of them is not certain by this except if God, Glorified is He, had no name other than those names. As for when His names, Glorified is He, are more than can be counted, the certainty of this is void, and it is best to limit oneself to what is in the Book of God and what is agreed upon as authentic after that, which is rare, while it is established that the names of God, the Exalted, are more than that transmitted, by necessity and by text. As for necessity, the Book of God contains more than that. As for text, there is the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "No servant whom distress or grief has afflicted says: 'O God, I am Your servant, son of Your servant, son of Your maidservant; my forelock is in Your hand, Your judgment over me is executed, Your decree over me is just. I ask You by every name that is Yours, which You named Yourself with, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to one of Your creation, or kept hidden in the knowledge of the unseen, that You make the Qur'an the spring of my heart, the light of my chest, the removal of my grief, and the departure of my distress and anxiety,' except that God removes his distress and anxiety, and replaces his grief with joy." Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Awanah in his (Sahih), Abu Ya'la and al-Bazzar. End.

Then al-Yamani began to mention what he found of the names stated explicitly, without turning to imitation. See him in (Iythar al-Haqq), for he refined the research with a noble approach.

Third: One of the commentators of the Zaydiyyah said regarding His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿so call upon Him by them﴾: the meaning is "name Him by them." In this is a command to invoke Him by the Most Beautiful Names. It is a command of recommendation (nadb) if it is taken to mean recitation by the ninety-nine, and the hadith urged this from him (ﷺ). If what is meant by naming is by those names which contain praise, not those which contain deviation, then it is obligatory.

Fourth: Al-Sayyid al-Yamani said in (Iythar al-Haqq): Is it permissible to call the praiseworthy attributes of the Lord, the Exalted, and His Most Beautiful Names "attributes" (sifat) of Him, Glorified and Exalted?

God, the Exalted, said: ﴿To God belongs the Highest Likeness﴾ [al-Nahl: 60]. The people of tafsir and lexicography mentioned that it is the Highest Description. Likewise it came in the words of Ali, peace be upon him, that he said: "So upon you, O questioner, is what the Qur'an indicates of His attributes" — mentioned by al-Sayyid Abu Talib in (al-Amali) with his chain, and al-Sayyid al-Radi in (Nahj al-Balagha), both in his reply, peace be upon him, to the one who said to him: "Describe for us the Fire of our Lord." This does not contradict the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Glory be to Him above what they describe﴾ [al-An'am: 100], because He did not declare His Essence free from description absolutely, so that good description would be included; rather He is exalted above their describing Him with falsehood and ugliness. End. And His, the Exalted, saying:

Commentary on the Words of Allah, Exalted is He:

[181] ﴿And among those whom We have created is a nation that guides by the truth and by it establishes justice.﴾

"﴿And among those whom We have created﴾" means: for Paradise, because it stands in contrast to ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind﴾ [al-A'raf: 179] (said by al-Nasafi).

"﴿a nation that guides by the truth﴾" means: they call to it.

"﴿and by it establishes justice﴾" means: they act upon it and judge by it. It has come in the reports that the intended "nation" is this Muhammadan nation. Qatadah said: "We have been told that the Prophet ﷺ, whenever he recited this verse, would say: 'This is for you, and the people before you have been given something similar.'"

On the authority of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, concerning this verse, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, among my nation there will be a people upon the truth until 'Isa ibn Maryam descends, whenever he descends." In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Mu'awiyah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A group of my nation will continue to be upon the truth, prevailing; those who forsake them will not harm them, nor will those who oppose them, until the Hour comes." In another narration: "until the command of Allah comes while they are upon that."

Al-Shihab said: The verse has been cited as evidence that consensus (ijma') is a proof in every age, and that no age is free of a mujtahid (qualified jurist) until the Hour is established.

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil), on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[182] ﴿And those who denied Our signs – We will lead them step by step from where they do not know.﴾

﴿And those who denied Our signs – We will lead them step by step from where they do not know.﴾ That is: We will seize them with punishment from a path they do not know, or We will open for them of circumstances what suits their desires, and then We will destroy them. The origin of istidraj (gradual leading, gradual drawing toward ruin): that one proceeds toward a thing little by little, likened to one who ascends a step at a time until he reaches the height. It was said: its origin is from the "daraj" (folded scroll), as though he folds one station after another, just as a scroll is folded. It was also said: it is from "daraja" (a degree), so that it means he descends degree after degree until he reaches the state of destruction.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[183] ﴿And I give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.﴾

"﴿And I give them respite﴾ meaning: I grant them a delay so that they may increase in sin." "﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾ meaning: strong and severe."

The ones addressed by this address are the disbelievers of Mecca.

In (al-Tanwir) it is said: they are Abu Jahl and his companions who mocked, whom Allah seized with His punishment on the day of (Uhud), destroying each one of them with a destruction different from that of his companion. End of quote.

And the saying of Allah, exalted is He, indicates:

"The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[184] ﴿Have they not reflected? There is no madness in their companion. He is only a clear warner.﴾

"﴿Have they not reflected that there is no madness in their companion?﴾ That is, as they fabricate [such claims]. The interrogative is for denunciation and rebuke: Have they not reflected that he—who is the greatest of the guiding community with the truth—is not in any way possessed? It is also permissible that the speech ends at His saying ﴿Have they not reflected?﴾, as a denunciation of their failure to reflect upon his affair, which is contingent upon his truthfulness and the soundness of his prophethood. Then the negation of madness from him is begun, as a matter of wonder and reproach.

(p-2915) And (al-jinnah) is a verbal noun, like al-jilsah, meaning insanity. It is not meant as the jinn, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿from among the jinn and mankind﴾ [al-Nas: 6], because that would require an elided genitive construction, i.e., "a jinn touched him or its frenzy." The expression of him ﷺ as (ṣāḥibihim) ("their companion") serves to indicate that their long association with him makes them aware of his freedom from what has been mentioned, so it contains emphasis on the denial and intensifies it. ﴿He is only a clear warner﴾, that is, a messenger who warns, ﴿clear﴾, that is, one who makes his warning plain, for the sake of exaggerating in establishing the proof against them. When He censured them for their reflection on his affair ﷺ, He denounced their neglect of contemplating the cosmic signs placed in the horizons and in the selves, which bear witness to the soundness of the revealed signs. So He, glorified is He, said:"

"Concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[185] ﴿Have they not considered the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and whatever things Allah has created, and that it may be that their term has drawn near? So in what statement after this will they believe?﴾

"﴿Have they not considered﴾, i.e., a considering of reasoning (nazar istidlal)." "﴿in the dominion of the heavens﴾: of the sun, the moon, the stars, and the clouds. And al-malakut (the dominion): the great kingdom." "﴿and the earth﴾, i.e., and in the dominion of the earth: of the seas, the mountains, the creatures, and the trees." "﴿and whatever things Allah has created﴾, i.e., and in what Allah has created of that to which the name (thing) (shay') applies, of kinds that number cannot count and description cannot encompass." "﴿and that it may be that their term has drawn near﴾ is coordinated with (malakut). I.e., there is the possibility that they may perish soon, thus departing from the world while in the most wretched of states." "﴿So in what statement after this﴾, i.e., the Qur'an," "﴿will they believe?﴾, i.e., if they do not believe in it, and it is the inimitable (mu'jiz) that comprises everything that yields guidance. In this is a definitive cutting off of the possibility of their belief altogether, and a total negation of it."

Note (tanbih):

Al-Jashami said: The verse indicates the obligation of reflecting upon the evidences, and that it is the path to knowledge. It also indicates that there is nothing one reflects upon except that through it Allah, exalted is He, is known."

(p-٢٩١٦)The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[186] ﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is none to guide him. And He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾

" ﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is none to guide him. And He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ That is, in their disbelief they are bewildered. The meaning is that whoever has been decreed misguidance, no one can guide him, and neither reflection nor warning benefits him, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: Look at what is in the heavens and the earth. But signs and warnings avail not a people who will not believe.﴾ [Yunus: 101] ﴿And whomever Allah intends to test, you will not possess for him anything from Allah.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 41]

The discussion of the words of God Most High:

[187] ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it take place? Say: "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None but He will reveal it at its time. It is heavy upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except suddenly." They ask you as if you were well-informed about it. Say: "Its knowledge is only with God, but most of the people do not know."﴾

"﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾" That is, about its establishment and its time. "﴿When will it take place?﴾" That is, when is its mooring (ersa'uha), or the time of its mooring, i.e., its fixing and settling. Ruww (mooring/anchoring) is used of heavy bodies, and its application to abstract meanings is by way of likening them to bodies.

"﴿Say: "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None but He will reveal it at its time"﴾" That is: none but He will manifest it at its time. "﴿It is heavy upon the heavens and the earth﴾" That is, it is great and momentous for their inhabitants, because of its terror and what it contains of reckoning and recompense; or, the knowledge of its time is heavy upon their inhabitants; or, its description is grave upon the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, from the scattering of the stars, the folding up of the sun, and the moving of the mountains. "﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly﴾" That is, unexpectedly, at a moment of your heedlessness.

"﴿They ask you as if you were well-informed about it﴾" That is: as if you were knowing of it. "﴿Say: "Its knowledge is only with God, but most of the people do not know"﴾" That is, its knowledge is with God; He has not given it to any of His creation.

A subtle point:

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you say, "Why did He repeat 'They ask you' and 'Its knowledge is only with God'?" I say: for emphasis, and what came with it of the addition of His saying "as if you were well-informed about it" [adds to this]. On this basis is the repetition of skilled scholars in their books: they do not leave the repeated element without an additional benefit. End.

And al-Nasir said in al-Insaf: In this type of repetition there is a nuance not found except in the Mighty Book, which is too exalted to be matched in it. That is because the custom in repetitions of this kind is that when a speech is built upon a purpose, and an incidental matter intervenes in its course, and one wishes to return to complete the first purpose after its distance in time, the mention of the first purpose is renewed, so that its end connects with its beginning. Examples of this have preceded in the Mighty Book, and more will come, and this is one of them. When He began the speech with "﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it take place?﴾", then interposed the answer contained in "﴿Say: its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾" up to "﴿suddenly﴾", the intention was to complete their question about it with an aspect of rebuke directed at them, which is contained in "﴿as if you were well-informed about it﴾", which is closely tied to the question. Since its distance in time had grown, its mention was renewed with a general renewal, and we never see it renewed except with a kind of summary, like a reminder of the first, needing no detailed restatement given what preceded. Hence it is said: "﴿They ask you﴾" without mentioning the thing asked about, which is "the Hour," being content with what preceded. When He repeated the question for this benefit, He also repeated the answer in summary, saying: "﴿Say: its knowledge is only with God﴾". This is noticed in the summary of a speech after its expansion. Among the most subtle things the Arabs noticed in this pattern of repetition, due to the distance of time, to renew the mention, is the verse:

*"Hasten this for us, and join us to that fat (shahm) one, for we have indeed grown weary of it, bajal."*

That is, only; he mentioned the alif and lam as a closing for the first of the two hemistichs, then when he began the second, he considered the first far off and renewed its mention, while leaving the first in its place. Hence Ibn Jinni inferred that what is of the verse on three feet is a complete line, not a half, as Abu al-Hasan held.

He said: Had it been a single line, the reference to the first would not have been distant, and there would be no need to repeat it. Do you not see that 'Ubayd, when he came with a long qasida and made the end of the first hemistich "al", did not repeat it at the start of the second hemistich, because it is a single line, so he did not regard its reference as distant? That is the saying of 'Ubayd ibn al-Abras al-Asadi:

*"O my two companions, halt and inquire of the abode, the dwelling of al-Hilal, its people having departed,*
*like the crushing of a cloak, after you the rain has effaced its habitation, and the north wind's returning."*

"Arba'a": stay. "Al-Hilal": a woman's name. "Sahq al-burd": he means like a worn-out, crushed cloak, i.e., decayed. "'Affa" with shedda: erased. "Al-qatr": rain. "Maghnahu": the place where they used to dwell. "Al-shamal" (with fatha or kasra) is a wind, that which blows from the sunrise and the Bana Na'sh direction, and it hardly blows at night; "ta'wibuha" is its blowing throughout the day. Then he continued in this manner for about a dozen lines. Consider this nuance, how the Arabs took great care of it, to the extent that they made the near seem distant and the short seem long. Ponder it, for it is a treasure, spent only among the skilled masters in the two arts of Arabic and eloquence. And God is the Helper. End.

The full qasida is in *Mukhtarat Ibn al-Shajari*, p. 37.

Then God Most High commanded him to declare his complete servitude, by that which indicates his inability to know the Hour, saying, glorified is He: ...

"The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[188] ﴿Say: I have no power to bring benefit to myself or to ward off harm, except what Allah wills. Had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much of good, and no evil would have touched me. I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe.﴾

"﴿Say: I have no power to bring benefit to myself or to ward off harm﴾ meaning: I am not able, for my own sake, to bring about any benefit or to repel any harm. ﴿Except what Allah wills﴾ meaning: His granting me that power by inspiring me with it, enabling me to do it, and empowering me over it. This is like His words, exalted is He, in Surat Yunus: ﴿And they say, 'When will this promise be, if you are truthful?'﴾ [Yunus: 48] ﴿Say: I have no power to bring harm to myself or benefit, except what Allah wills. For every nation is a term﴾ [Yunus: 49]. ﴿Had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much of good﴾ meaning: of benefit, by arranging its causes, so that I would, for example, store up for the year of drought from the year of plenty, and for the time of high prices from the time of low prices. ﴿And no evil would have touched me﴾ meaning: no harm, by guarding against its causes. ﴿I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings﴾ meaning: I am a servant who has been sent as a warner and a bringer of good tidings, and it is not part of my role that I know the unseen. As for His words, exalted is He, ﴿to a people who believe﴾, it is permissible for it to be connected to ﴿bringer of good tidings﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 19] alone, while the object of ﴿warner﴾ is omitted, meaning: to the disbelievers, and it is omitted because it is known. And al-Shihab said: so that the tongue is purified of them."

Then the Exalted explained the enormity of the disbelievers' offense in their audacity toward associating partners with God, by reminding them of the beginnings of their own circumstances, which contradict this, in His, glorified be He, saying:

The discussion on the interpretation of His, Exalted is He, saying:

[189] ﴿It is He who created you from one soul and made from it its mate that he might find tranquility in her. And when he covered her, she bore a light burden and carried it about. But when she became heavy, they called upon Allah, their Lord, "If You give us a righteous [child], we will surely be among the grateful."﴾

" ﴿It is He who created you from one soul﴾ and it is the soul of Adam (peace be upon him). " ﴿And made from it its mate﴾ meaning, of its own kind, as in His, Exalted is He, saying: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves﴾ [al-Rum: 21]. " ﴿That he might find tranquility in her﴾ meaning, that he might be at ease with her and incline toward her, and not shun her, because a kind inclines toward its own kind more, and is more familiar with it. And when she is a part of him, the tranquility and affection are more intense, just as a person finds tranquility in his child and loves him with affection because he is a part of him. And He mentioned " ﴿that he might find tranquility﴾ " after feminine forms in His saying " one " and " ﴿from it its mate﴾ ", going back to the meaning of " soul ", to clarify that what is meant by it is Adam. Moreover, the male is the one who finds tranquility in the female and covers her, so the masculine form is more fitting in correspondence with the meaning (tabaq). This was stated by al-Zamakhshari. " ﴿When he covered her﴾ meaning, he had intercourse with her. The word (taghashshi, covering) is a kinayah (euphemism/allusion) for intercourse, and likewise ghashayan and ityan.

" ﴿She bore a light burden﴾ meaning, it was light upon her, and that is at the beginning of the pregnancy, when the woman feels no pain from it, for it is only a drop (nutfah), then a clot (ʿalaqah), then a lump of flesh (mudghah). " ﴿And carried it about﴾ meaning, she continued with it, light, and stood and sat. " ﴿But when she became heavy﴾ meaning: she became one with weight, because of the largeness of the child in her womb. " ﴿They called upon Allah, their Lord, "If You give us a righteous [child]﴾ meaning, a sound child whose body is healthy, or a boy. " ﴿We will surely be among the grateful﴾ meaning, for Your blessings, of which this blessing is one.

﴿فَلَمّا آتاهُما صالِحًا﴾ [When He gave them a righteous child]. Meaning: as they had requested. ﴿جَعَلا لَهُ شُرَكاءَ فِيما آتاهُما﴾ [they made partners for Him in what He had given them]. Meaning: they failed in gratitude in the most wretched way, in return for the blessing of a righteous child, when they substituted association (shirk) for it. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿فَتَعالى اللَّهُ عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ [Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him], is a declaration of His transcendence, carrying the sense of wonder.

Note (tanbih):

This verse was revealed as a rebuke to the polytheists for their crime of shirk and their breaking of their covenant, in that they acted contrary to what they had pledged to Allah. Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the blessings He bestowed upon them: that He created them from a single soul (nafs wahidah), made their spouses from themselves so that they might find comfort in them, then brought them into being after the covering (of the wife), progressing them through the stages of creation from non-existence to existence and from weakness to strength. Then He stated that they gave their pledges that if He granted them what they sought and gave them the children they desired, they would surely be among the grateful. Then He informed of their treachery and ingratitude for these blessings, by which He, glorified is He, had favored them, and of their breaking of their covenant to single Him out with gratitude, (p-٢٩٢١) in that they associated others with Him in that.

A parallel to this verse, in reporting the polytheists' transformation of Allah's blessing into disbelief, is His saying in Surat Yunus: ﴿He it is who makes you travel on land and sea, until when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it, there comes upon them a violent wind and the waves come at them from every place, and they think they are encompassed, they call upon Allah, sincerely devoted to Him in religion: "If You save us from this, we will surely be among the grateful."﴾ [Yunus: 22] ﴿But when He saves them, at once they commit injustice in the earth without right﴾ [Yunus: 23]. The exegetes have mentioned here hadiths and reports (athar) which convey that the intended subject of this context is Adam and Eve. We have no need to narrate them, for their chains are weak and defective, as the memorizer Ibn Kathir (al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir) demonstrated in his Tafsir.

The acceptance and transmission of these by a group of the early generations (al-salaf) does not benefit their authenticity in any way, since their origin is taken from the fabricated tales of the People of the Book (ahl al-kitab), as Ibn Kathir proved. As for some people's exaggeration that they are derived from the niche of prophethood (mishkat al-nubuwwah), because so-and-so and so-and-so narrated them, that is the embellishment of words to tear apart meanings, for the prophetic niche is too exalted for anything to be drawn from it except what is known for its excellence.

Having known this, it becomes clear to you that whoever relied upon those hadiths and reports, and went to the view that the intended "single soul" and its partner are Adam and Eve, then raised an objection against himself that they are both innocent of shirk, and that the apparent wording requires it, then began to interpret it, either by supposing an omitted genitive (idafah), that is, that their offspring made partners for Him in what He had given their offspring, or by saying that the intention is the making of one of them, namely Eve, through the use of the dual for the singular, or by some other means, then he has gone off in a direction other than the right one.

Several scholars have affirmed what we have adopted as the meaning of the verse. Al-Hasan al-Basri said, as Ibn Jarir reported from him: the verse means the descendants of Adam, and whoever among them associated others after him. In another report from him: this occurred among some of the religious communities (milal), and it did not concern Adam.

Ibn Kathir said: the chains to al-Hasan regarding the explanation of this are sound, and it is among the best of the tafsirs and the most fitting meaning for the verse.

(p-٢٩٢٢) He said: Had the raised (marfu') hadith that it concerns Adam and Eve been preserved with him from the narration of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), neither he nor anyone else would have turned away from it, especially given his piety and scrupulousness. This indicates that it, if it is authentic, is a statement halted at the Companion (mawquf), not raised to the Prophet. End of quote.

Al-Qaffal said: Allah, exalted is He, mentioned this story by way of a parable (tamthil wa darb al-mathal), and to show that this condition is the image of the condition of these polytheists in their ignorance and their claim of shirk. The sense of this statement is as if He, exalted is He, were saying: It is He who created each one of you from a single soul, and made from its kind its spouse, a human being equal to him in humanity. When the husband covered his wife and the pregnancy appeared, the husband and wife called upon their Lord: "If You give us a righteous, sound child, we will surely be among those who give thanks for Your blessings and favors." Then when Allah gave them a righteous, sound child, the husband and wife made partners for Allah in what He had given them, because at times they attribute that child to natural causes, as is the saying of the naturalists (al-tabi'iyyun), at times to the stars, as is the saying of the astrologers (al-munajjimun), and at times to idols and images, as is the saying of the idol-worshippers.

Al-Nasir (Ibn al-Munayyir) said in al-Intisaf, critiquing al-Zamakhshari: The safest and nearest (to the truth), and Allah knows best, is that the intended meaning is the two sexes, male and female, without specifying a particular individual. The meaning, and Allah knows best, seems to be: He created you as one kind, and also made your spouses from you, so that you might find rest in them. Then when the kind which is male covered the other kind which is female, such and such occurred between these two kinds. He attributed this statement to the kind (as a whole), even though among them there were monotheists, in the manner of the saying "the Banu so-and-so killed a man," meaning attributing what some of them did to all of them.

Benefit (fa'idah):

Some of the Zaydi exegetes said: The fruit of this verse is that when Allah said: ﴿When she became heavy﴾ [al-A'raf: 189], He made the state of heaviness differ from what preceded it, and that supplication is specifically appropriate in it because it is a state of fear. Al-Hadi held that when a pregnant woman has reached six months of pregnancy, her dispositions are like those of a sick person, and her dispositions take effect from a third (of her estate). This is also the view of Malik and al-Layth, and they cited the verse as evidence, because Allah distinguished between the state of lightness and the state of heaviness. Others said: her dispositions are fully valid, so long as the labor pains have not seized her. We say: it is permissible for her, after six months, to give birth at any time. End of quote.

Then he said: The verse indicates that it is permissible to supplicate for the seeking of worldly matters, and that the attainment of a child is a favor which requires gratitude for it. End of quote.

Then Allah, exalted is He, resumed the rebuke of all the polytheists, and the condemnation of their associating others with Him, and the complete nullification of it, by explaining the nature of what they associated with Him, glorified is He, and detailing its conditions, which necessarily entail the falsity of what they believed concerning Him, through His saying, glorified is He.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 7, verse 191:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[191] ﴿Do they associate with Him those who create nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾

"﴿Do they associate﴾": that is, with the Creator of things, exalted and sanctified is He. "﴿Those who create nothing﴾": that is, who have no power to create anything at all, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, a parable is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke other than Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ [al-Hajj: 73]. That is: whoever has such an attribute, how can he be worshipped? It is necessarily the right of the one who is worshipped to be the creator of his worshipper. "﴿While they themselves are created﴾": that is, rather, they are created and made, as the Friend (Khalil, i.e., Ibrahim), upon him be blessings and peace, said: ﴿Do you worship what you carve?﴾ [al-Saffat: 95].

The discussion of His words, exalted is He:

[192] ﴿And they are not able to help them, nor can they help themselves.﴾

"﴿And they are not able to help them﴾" i.e., their worshippers, when a matter afflicts them. "﴿help﴾" i.e., by bringing about a benefit or repelling a harm. "﴿nor can they help themselves﴾" when some calamity of the calamities befalls them, as He, exalted is He, said: (p-2924) ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them a thing, they could not retrieve it from it﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], and as al-Khalil (peace be upon him) used to break the idols of his people and humiliate them to the utmost degree of humiliation.

Ibn Kathir has related that Mu'adh ibn 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh and Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with them both, embraced Islam when the Prophet (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, and they were both young men. They used to run at night to the idols of the polytheists, breaking and destroying them, and taking them as firewood for widows, so that their people would take heed. 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh, who was a chief among his people, had an idol that he worshipped and perfumed, so the two of them would come at night, turn it upside down on its head, and smear it with filth. 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh would come, see what had been done to it, wash it and perfume it, and place a sword beside it, saying to it: "Defend yourself." Then they would return to doing the same, and he would return to his practice again. Until they took it once, tied it together with a dead dog, and lowered it by a rope into a well there. When 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh came and saw that, he looked and knew that the religion he had been upon was false. And he said:

By Allah, if you were a god, you would not be, you and the dog, together in one rope.

(mustadann: humbled and enslaved. Qaran: a rope.)

Then he embraced Islam, and his Islam was good, and he was martyred on the Day of Uhud, a martyr, may Allah be pleased with him and content him.

(See the Sirah of Ibn Hisham, vol. 2, p. 95, Halabi edition, and p. 303, Gottingen edition.)

Note: al-Jashami said: The verse indicates the validity of argumentation in religion, because His words "﴿Do they associate with Him that which creates nothing, and they are themselves created?﴾" [al-A'raf: 191] are an argument; and it indicates that the one deserving of worship is the One who creates, bestows favours, and has power over benefit and harm, which is Allah, exalted is He.

(p-2925) The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[193] ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for you whether you call them or you are silent.﴾

"﴿And if you call them﴾, O polytheists," "﴿to guidance﴾, that is, to that which contains right direction," "﴿they will not follow you﴾, that is, to what you desire and seek." "﴿It is the same for you whether you call them or you are silent﴾" means that these idols do not hear the supplication of whoever calls upon them, as Abraham said: ﴿O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and does not avail you at all?﴾ [Maryam: 42]

It is also permitted in this verse that the meaning be: "And if you call them to guide you and you ask them, as you ask Allah, for good and evil, they will not respond to you as Allah responds to you," in accordance with His words, exalted is He, afterward: ﴿So call upon them, and let them respond to you, if you are truthful﴾ [al-A'raf: 194].

The commentary on the words of Allah, Exalted is He:

[194] ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah are servants like you. So call upon them, and let them respond to you, if you should be truthful.﴾

"﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah﴾, that is, those you worship and name as gods," "﴿are servants like you﴾, that is, created beings similar to you." "﴿So call upon them﴾ is a command of incapacitation and rebuke. That is: call upon them to bring about a benefit or to remove a harm." "﴿and let them respond to you, if you should be truthful﴾, that is, in your claim that they are gods."

And the words of Allah, Exalted is He:

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[195] ﴿Do they have feet with which they walk? Or do they have hands with which they strike? Or do they have eyes with which they see? Or do they have ears with which they hear? Say: Call upon your partners, then plot against me, and give me no respite.﴾

"﴿Do they have feet with which they walk? Or do they have hands with which they strike? Or do they have eyes with which they see (p-2926) Or do they have ears with which they hear?﴾" This is rebuke upon rebuke, confirming what the challenge of incapacity (al-amr al-ta'jizi) implies, namely non-response, by showing the total lack of their instruments. For responsiveness belongs to bodily forms only when they have life and motive and perceptive powers; whatever lacks any of these is entirely incapable of action. It is as if it were said: Do they have these instruments through which response is realized, so that their response to you could be possible? He directed the denial at each of these four instruments separately, as a repetition of the rebuke, a doubling of the reproach, and an indication that the absence of each one individually suffices to show the impossibility of response. Abu al-Su'ud related this.

It is said: since He made them like them (the worshippers), He reversed the equality by pointing out what they lack, because they are inferior to them, and worshipping one who is like oneself is not fitting, so how much less one who is below.

Note: al-Razi said: Some ignorant and foolish anthropomorphists (al-Mushabbihah) clung to this verse to affirm these organs for God Most High. They said: God made the absence of these organs in these idols a proof of their not being deities; so if these organs did not exist in God Most High, their absence would be a proof of non-divinity, and that is false; therefore it is necessary to affirm these organs for God Most High... etc.

I say: The apparent point of those who affirm them is that their absence indicates deficiency, which is impossible for the Lord Most High, since He possesses every attribute of perfection. It is well known that in affirming them for Him there are other verses and well-known hadiths that suffice without the strain of deriving them for Him from a verse like this. But this is according to the Salafi method, which is affirmation without modality (takyif), for whoever gives modality has likened, and whoever denies has nullified. So the anthropomorphists are like the negators, and the truth lies beyond both of them, and the matter is well known.

When the Exalted made clear that their partners are powerless, He commanded His Messenger ﷺ to confront them in argument and to repeat the rebuke against them, so He said, glorified is He: ﴿Say: Call upon your partners﴾, i.e., seek their help against me, ﴿then plot against me﴾, i.e., work, you and they, for my destruction from where I do not perceive it, so that I may be able to repel it.

(p-2927) ﴿And give me no respite﴾, i.e., hasten in your scheme against me, and do not grant me a period in which I may gain knowledge of your plot, for I am not concerned with you. Nafi' and Abu 'Amr kept the yā' in "kīdūnī" (plot against me), while the rest omitted it. Similar is His saying: ﴿And give me no respite﴾ [Yunus: 71] and ﴿Then give me no respite﴾ [Hud: 55]. Al-Wahidi said: The point regarding this is that the fawasil (verse-endings) resemble qawafi (rhyme-endings), and they omitted these yā's when they fell at the rhyme, as in the verse:

*He touches the saddle-cloths in his dwelling with his two hands, like the Jew who prays*

(and its original is al-musalli).

Those who kept them, did so because the original is retention.

And His Exalted saying:

ON THE INTERPRETATION OF HIS WORDS, EXALTED IS HE:

[196] ﴿Indeed, my protector is Allah, who revealed the Book, and He is the protector of the righteous.﴾

"﴿Indeed, my protector is Allah, who revealed the Book﴾ is a justification for not being concerned, which is clearly understood from the context. That is: the One who takes charge of my protection and support is Allah, who sent down the Book, which contains these great and beneficial sciences."

Abu al-Su'ud said: Describing Him, exalted is He, as the one who sent down the Book serves to indicate the proof of His guardianship and to point to another reason for not being concerned, as if it were said: "I am not concerned about you and your partners, because my protector is Allah, who sent down the Book, which declares that He is my protector and supporter, and that your partners cannot even help themselves, let alone help you."

His words, exalted is He, ﴿and He is the protector of the righteous﴾ are a concluding statement that confirms what came before. That is: it is His custom to take charge of the righteous among His servants, to support them, and not to forsake them. And in it is an allusion, for those who lack righteousness, to abandonment and destruction.

al-Hasan al-Basri said: The polytheists used to frighten the Messenger (ﷺ) with their gods, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Call upon your partners﴾ [al-A'raf: 195], to the end of the verse, to make clear to you that they have no power to inflict any harm upon me in any way whatsoever. This is like what Hud (peace be upon him) said when his people said: ﴿We do not say except that some of our gods have struck you with evil.﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and bear witness that I am free from what you associate, [apart from Him]. So scheme against me, all of you, then give me no respite. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord﴾ [Hud: 54–56], to the end of the verse.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[197] ﴿And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.﴾

"﴿And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you﴾, i.e., they do not take up the cause of anyone, because they are not able to help you." ﴿Nor can they help themselves﴾, i.e., if someone intends to harm them.

The commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

[198] ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear. And you see them looking at you, yet they do not see.﴾

"﴿And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear.﴾ Because they have no hearing, even if you fashion ears for them, just as they have no sight, even if you fashion eyes for them. As He said: ﴿And you see them looking at you﴾, when you fashion eyes for them. ﴿Yet they do not see.﴾ Because they are inanimate objects, they are treated as those who have intellect, so He refers to them with the pronoun for rational beings, since they are in the shapes of humans that have been fashioned. This is part of the completion of the reasoning, for His lack of concern with them, so there is no repetition."

Al-Suddi said: "What is meant by this is (the polytheists)." Something similar is related from Mujahid, meaning: even if they look at you, they gain no benefit from looking and seeing.

Ibn Kathir said: "The first (interpretation) is more preferable, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir and was also said by Qatada, to avoid the incoherence (tafkik) of the discourse, because the ones being spoken of are idols."

Note: Among the strange deductions of the Mu'tazila (a rationalist school of theology), their statement on this verse, in the words of al-Jashami, is of this kind: "The verse indicates that looking (nazar) is other than seeing (ru'yah), and that it does not necessitate seeing; for this reason He described them as looking without seeing."

He said: "Similar to this is their saying: 'I looked at the crescent moon but did not see it.' They divide looking into various kinds, but seeing is not divided."

He said: "Thus the view of those who say that His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 22] ﴿looking at their Lord﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 23] necessitates seeing is refuted." End of quotation.

It is not hidden that the original usage of the term "looking" (nazar) is seeing and perceiving (ibsar), and for this reason they alternate in this meaning and are often synonymous. Its separation from seeing in this verse is due to the indication that the ones being spoken of are inanimate objects. There is no indication in the verse that would allow this to be analogized to other cases, let alone the authentic reports regarding its occurrence, which serve as its explanation. Understand this well.

Then Allah, exalted is He, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to pardon the polytheists when they argue with him about their partners after this clarification, by His saying, glorified is He:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[199] ﴿Take what is pardoned, enjoin what is customary, and turn away from the ignorant.﴾

"﴿Take what is pardoned﴾" meaning: in place of anger, so that they will be more receptive to advice. "﴿And enjoin what is customary﴾" meaning: with what is good and approved of among actions, for such things are close to being accepted by people without objection. Since the one who advises others is like one exposed to their hostility, He mentioned the third thing that he needs in this regard, saying: "﴿And turn away from the ignorant﴾," meaning: those who persist in their ignorance. So do not repay fools with the like of their foolishness, do not dispute with them, be forbearing toward them, and overlook what they do that hurts you.

Two Reminders:

The first: Some scholars said: The secret of the Shariah in natural dispositions and customs is the affirmation of what is approved (p-2930) and the erasure of what is disapproved. To this points His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾ [Luqman: 17]. For what is "right" (ma'ruf) is what sound natures recognize and find good, and what is "wrong" (munkar) is what they reject and find ugly. This is because the ultimate aim of the Shariah is the ease of creation in a state and order that are reasonable. Therefore it is not valid to rule for the uniformity of customs in all lands. End quote.

The second: It is narrated from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) with noble character, and there is no verse in the Qur'an more comprehensive of noble character than this one.

Al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn said to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: "Hey, son of al-Khattab! By Allah, you do not give us abundantly, nor do you judge among us with justice." 'Umar became angry, to the point that he intended to strike him. Al-Hurr ibn Qays said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful! Allah, Exalted, said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Take what is pardoned, enjoin what is customary, and turn away from the ignorant﴾, and this man is among the ignorant."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "By Allah! 'Umar did not go beyond it once he recited it to him, and he was one who stopped at the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 7, verse 200:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[200] ﴿And if an evil prompting from Satan should incite you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

"﴿And if an evil prompting from Satan should incite you﴾ meaning: if a whisper from Satan should afflict you, one that stirs up your anger at their ignorance and their wrongdoing, and drives you to act contrary to what you were commanded regarding pardon and enjoining what is good." "﴿Then seek refuge in Allah﴾ meaning: seek protection in Him, and call upon Him to repel it." "﴿Indeed, He is Hearing﴾ meaning: of your supplication." "﴿Knowing﴾ meaning: of your seeking refuge."

Al-Zamakhshari said: "Al-nazgh" and "al-nasgh" both mean goading and pricking, as if he (Satan) pricks people when he incites them to acts of disobedience. That is, his whispering and incitement are likened to goading, which is the insertion of a needle or the tip of a stick or something similar into the hide, as a driver does to urge on the animals. Making the nazgh itself the one who "goads" is a metaphor by attribution, by making the verbal noun the agent, like "a grandfather's grandfather" (jaddi jaddihi).

Abu al-Su'ud said: In the command to seek refuge in Allah, exalted is He, there is an emphasis on the gravity of the matter and an alert that it is among the formidable calamities from which one cannot be freed from its harm except by taking refuge in the sanctuary of His protection, mighty and majestic is He.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[201] ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an impulse from Satan touches them, remember [Allah], and at once they are seeing clearly.﴾
